# ColivEase: full guides

> ColivEase is a Toronto rental platform built around roommates: a rule-based match score from area and commute, budget, move-in date, student or worker, gender preference and shared language; teams that apply together; optional ID verification badges and licensed-agent badges; every listing reviewed by a person; scam-line warnings in chat; neighbourhood scores with commute times, and whole homes you can rent room by room.

- Serves renters, roommates and landlords in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Ontario, Canada, only.
- Roommate match score from area and commute, budget, move-in date, student or worker, gender preference (can be a must-have) and shared language. It follows fixed rules, not AI, and profile summaries are written from a fixed template. Roommates can form teams of 2 to 5 and apply for a home together.
- Language communities: roommates and homes rented room by room are shown to people who share at least one language with them; whole homes are open to everyone, with your own language community first. The app is available in 10 languages (English, Chinese, Korean, Spanish, French, Hindi/Punjabi, Vietnamese, Tagalog, Persian, Portuguese).
- Privacy first: profiles can use a comic avatar; each person decides, photo by photo and person by person, who sees a real photo and can take it back. A home's exact address stays hidden (maps show a ~350 m area) until the host accepts an application.
- Safety: every new listing is reviewed by a person before it goes live; scam lines in chat (such as "send the deposit first") trigger a warning; listings, people and messages can be reported or blocked; optional ID verification (Stripe ID, phone and email) gives a badge; licensed agents are checked against RECO and get a badge.
- ColivEase never handles rent or deposits: tenants and hosts arrange payment between themselves.
- Every listing shows neighbourhood scores (transit, amenities, safety, schools) and commute times, and whether the host lives in the home.
- Landlords can rent a whole home room by room (group renting): each room has its own photos and rent, renters apply for a specific room or as a team, and current roommates can be shown on the listing.
- Landlord mode is reviewed: hosts apply and are approved, usually within 48 hours, before they can post homes; owner-direct landlords can have 3 live listings for free.
- Prices in CAD, plus 13% HST: a free account (profile, match scores, homes, chat, scam warnings, 1 team); Gold membership $19.99/month and Diamond $29.99/month (more teams, an animated profile frame, a higher place in people search); optional ID verification $9.99 for 3 years; AI lease check $4.99 per lease (same price for members); pinned listing $49.99 for 30 days; tenant invite pack $29.99 for 10 invites; licensed-agent plans $199.99/month (5 listings) or $299.99/month (10 listings).
- Sign in with Google, Apple or an email link; you must be 18 or older. Without an account you can browse homes. Free on the web at https://www.colivease.ca/app.html; iOS and Android apps are on the way. Guides are in English and Chinese.

# Best Websites to Find a Room in Toronto: Honest Guide

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/best-rental-websites-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

The best websites to find a room in Toronto, compared honestly: listing sites, Kijiji vs Facebook Marketplace, student boards, roommate apps and scam risk.

The best websites to find a room in Toronto depend on what you're after: big listing sites like Rentals.ca and Zumper are strongest for whole apartments, Kijiji and Facebook Marketplace have the most rooms in shared houses, and school housing boards and roommate platforms are built for students and people who want to share. Most renters use two or three at once. The real skill is spotting which listings are genuine, because scam risk varies a lot from one platform to the next.

## Key takeaways

- **Use a mix:** one big listing site, one roommate or student platform, and one community channel.
- **Kijiji and Facebook Marketplace** have huge volume but the least verification, so they need the most caution.
- **Student boards** such as Places4Students and your school's own service are a good first stop if you're enrolled.
- **Chinese-language channels** (51.ca, YorkBBS, Xiaohongshu, WeChat groups) are fast and convenient but carry real scam risk.
- **On any platform:** confirm the landlord, view the unit, and never pay before you sign.

## Toronto rental websites at a glance

This table reflects how each type of platform generally works. Features change, so check each site's current terms.

| Platform type | Examples | Best for | What to watch for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Large listing sites | Rentals.ca, Zumper, PadMapper | Whole apartments and condos, map search, comparing buildings | Fewer single rooms; condo listings may be posted by agents |
| Verified-listing platforms | liv.rent | Renters who want ID-checked landlords and a reusable profile | Smaller selection of rooms than open classifieds |
| Open classifieds | Kijiji, Craigslist | Rooms in houses, basements, private landlords | Anyone can post; fake and duplicate ads are common |
| Social media | Facebook Marketplace and groups | Rooms, sublets, last-minute moves | Fake profiles, pressure tactics, no verification |
| Student housing boards | Places4Students, school off-campus services | Students near campus, shorter terms | Usually limited to enrolled students; still check the landlord |
| Chinese community channels | 51.ca, YorkBBS, Xiaohongshu, WeChat groups | Chinese-speaking landlords and roommates | Impersonation and deposit scams, especially before school starts |

## The big listing sites

### Rentals.ca

Rentals.ca is one of the largest Canadian listing sites, with many purpose-built rental buildings, condos and houses. It also publishes the monthly National Rent Report with Urbanation, which is handy for checking whether an asking rent is reasonable. It's strongest for whole units; if you only want a room, you'll find fewer options.

### Zumper and PadMapper

Zumper bought PadMapper in 2016, and both are map-first search tools. They're useful for seeing what's available around a subway line or campus at a glance. As with any aggregator, double-check that a listing is still live before you get attached.

### liv.rent

liv.rent says it verifies landlord identity and checks listings before they go live, and lets renters build a reusable profile for applications. That extra layer of checking appeals to cautious renters, though the selection of single rooms is narrower than on the open classifieds.

## Kijiji vs Facebook Marketplace rentals

These two carry a large share of Toronto's room listings, especially rooms in houses, basement units and sublets from private landlords. They have a lot in common, but there are differences worth knowing.

| | Kijiji | Facebook Marketplace and groups |
|---|---|---|
| Typical listings | Rooms, basements, whole units from private landlords | Rooms, sublets, short-term stays, roommate-wanted posts |
| Who you're dealing with | Often anonymous until you message | A personal profile, which can be real or newly created |
| Search | Filters by price, location and type | Marketplace filters plus many separate neighbourhood or school groups |
| Biggest risk | Copied photos from other listings, too-good-to-be-true prices | Fake profiles, "I'm overseas, send a deposit and I'll mail the keys" |
| Best habit | Reverse-search the photos, ask for a live video walkthrough | Check the profile's age and history, never pay before viewing |

**Craigslist** works much like Kijiji but routes messages through an anonymous email relay, which makes it harder to confirm who you're talking to. Use the same caution.

Our full guide to [rental scams in Toronto](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) walks through the most common tricks and what to do if you've already paid.

## Student housing boards

If you're enrolled at a college or university, start here. Many Ontario colleges partner with **Places4Students**, an off-campus housing listing service; Seneca, for example, says it partners with it. Universities such as U of T and York run their own off-campus housing services. Benefits include listings aimed at students, shorter terms that line up with semesters, and sometimes staff who can give advice if a problem comes up. Schools generally don't inspect listings, though, so verify the landlord and the unit just as you would anywhere else.

## Roommate apps Toronto renters use

Roommate platforms focus on the people, not just the room. They help when you're new to the city, want to rent a whole house with others, or care about who you'll share a kitchen with.

What to look for in a roommate platform:

- [ ] **Matching on lifestyle**, not just budget: sleep schedule, cleanliness, guests, smoking, pets
- [ ] **Some form of verification** for users and landlords
- [ ] **Privacy controls**, so your photos and details aren't public by default
- [ ] **Clear information about the home**, including whether the landlord lives there
- [ ] **A way to apply as a group** if you're renting with friends

For tips on choosing well, see our guide to [finding a roommate in Toronto](/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/).

## Chinese-language channels

Many Chinese-speaking newcomers and students search on **51.ca**, **YorkBBS (约克论坛)**, **Xiaohongshu (RED)** and **WeChat groups**. They're fast, you can ask questions in your own language, and you'll often find roommates with similar routines. They're also where fake landlords, "second landlords" re-renting without permission and deposit scams cluster, especially in August and December before semesters start. Verify the person's identity on a live video call, confirm they own or manage the unit, and use the Ontario Standard Lease.

## How to use any rental site safely

1. **Search the address and photos.** Reverse-image search the pictures and look up the address to see if it's listed elsewhere at a different price.
2. **Confirm who you're dealing with.** Ask for the landlord's full legal name and check it against the lease. For condos, ask whether they're the owner or a licensed agent.
3. **See it before you pay.** View in person, or by live video where the person shows the street, building entrance and unit number.
4. **Sign first, pay second.** Most residential tenancies in Ontario use the Ontario Standard Lease. A rent deposit can't be more than one month's rent.
5. **Pay traceably.** Use e-transfer or cheque and get a receipt. Avoid cash, crypto, gift cards and wire transfers to strangers.

Before you go, print our [rental viewing checklist](/blog/rental-viewing-checklist-toronto/) so you know what to test on the day. When you're ready to apply, our [rental application guide](/blog/rental-application-toronto/) covers the documents landlords ask for.

## Find your place with fewer surprises

## FAQ

**Which rental site in Toronto has the fewest scams?**
No site is scam-free. Platforms that verify landlords or listings, and school housing boards that only accept registered landlords, add a layer of checking, while open classifieds and social media groups let anyone post in minutes. Whatever site you use, confirm who owns or manages the unit, view it in person or by live video, and never pay before signing a lease.

**Is Facebook Marketplace safe for renting in Toronto?**
It can be used safely, but it's one of the easiest places for fake listings because anyone can create a profile. Check how old the profile is, compare the photos with a reverse image search, and insist on seeing the unit before paying anything. Be especially wary of a landlord who says they're out of the country.

**Do I have to pay to use rental websites in Toronto?**
Most large listing sites are free for renters to browse and contact landlords, though some offer paid extras. Be cautious if anyone asks you to pay a fee just to see a unit's address or book a viewing. Check each platform's own terms before paying for anything.

**What is the best way for students to find housing in Toronto?**
Start with your school's off-campus housing service, then widen your search to listing sites and roommate platforms. School boards are built for students and some offer advice if something goes wrong. If you're still overseas, use live video viewings and never send a deposit for a place no one has verified.

## Sources

- [TechCrunch: Zumper acquires PadMapper (2016)](https://techcrunch.com/2016/02/25/zumper-acquires-padmapper-relaunches-it-with-updated-interface/)
- [Seneca: Off-campus housing](https://students.senecacollege.ca/spaces/106/off-campus-housing/home)

# 多伦多租房网站推荐：哪个平台靠谱？

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/best-rental-websites-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

多伦多租房网站推荐：Rentals.ca、Kijiji、Facebook、学校平台、室友app，以及51、约克论坛、小红书哪个靠谱？优缺点和防骗要点一次讲清。

多伦多租房网站推荐，没有标准答案，要看你找什么：找整套公寓，Rentals.ca、Zumper 这类大型网站最全；找合租单间，Kijiji 和 Facebook Marketplace 房源最多；在读学生先看学校的校外住房平台；想找合拍的室友，用室友匹配平台；习惯中文的话，51.ca、约克论坛、小红书和微信群沟通最方便。大多数人会同时用两三个渠道，关键是学会分辨哪些房源是真的，因为不同平台的诈骗风险差别很大。

## 先看重点

- **组合使用**：一个大型租房网站 + 一个学生或室友平台 + 一个社区渠道。
- **Kijiji 和 Facebook** 房源多，但几乎没有审核，最需要小心。
- **在读学生**先用 Places4Students 或学校自己的校外住房服务。
- **中文渠道**方便快捷，但开学季假房源特别多。
- **不管哪个平台**：核实房东、亲眼看房、签约前不付钱。

## 多伦多找房平台一览

下表是各类平台的大致特点，功能会变，以平台现行规则为准。

| 平台类型 | 代表 | 适合 | 要注意 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 大型租房网站 | Rentals.ca、Zumper、PadMapper | 整套公寓、Condo、按地图找房 | 单间较少；Condo 常由中介发布 |
| 房源核实型平台 | liv.rent | 想要房东经过身份核实的租客 | 单间选择比分类网站少 |
| 分类广告 | Kijiji、Craigslist | 民房单间、地下室、个人房东 | 谁都能发帖，假房源和重复帖多 |
| 社交媒体 | Facebook Marketplace 和各类群组 | 单间、转租、临时找房 | 假账号、催你先付钱、无审核 |
| 学校租房平台 | Places4Students、学校校外住房服务 | 学校附近、按学期短租 | 一般限在读学生；房东仍要自己核实 |
| 中文社区渠道 | 51.ca、约克论坛、小红书、微信群 | 中文房东和室友 | 冒充房东、骗定金，开学前尤其多 |

## 英文主流租房网站

**Rentals.ca** 是加拿大规模较大的租房网站之一，出租公寓楼、Condo 和独立屋都有。它每月和 Urbanation 联合发布全国租金报告 (National Rent Report)，可以用来判断一个报价是否合理。找整套房很方便，单间相对少。

**Zumper 和 PadMapper**：Zumper 在2016年收购了 PadMapper，两者都以地图搜索为主，适合沿着地铁线或学校周边看看有什么房。聚合类网站的房源要多确认一下是否还在出租。

**liv.rent** 表示会核实房东身份、在房源上线前做审核，租客还可以建立一份可重复使用的申请资料。多一道审核对谨慎的租客有吸引力，但单间数量比不上分类网站。

**Kijiji 和 Facebook Marketplace** 是多伦多单间、地下室和转租房源最集中的地方，个人房东很多。Kijiji 上发帖人在你发消息前基本是匿名的，常见问题是盗用别人的房源照片、价格低得离谱；Facebook 上看得到个人主页，但主页可能是刚注册的假号，最典型的骗局是"我人在国外，先转定金，我把钥匙寄给你"。看到这类说法，直接放弃。**Craigslist** 和 Kijiji 类似，而且消息经过匿名邮件转发，更难确认对方身份。

## 学校租房平台：在读学生首选

很多安省学院和 **Places4Students** 合作提供校外房源，比如 Seneca 就说明与其合作；多大 (U of T)、约克大学等也有自己的校外住房服务。好处是房源面向学生、租期能对上学期，有的还有工作人员提供咨询。不过学校一般不会实地检查房源，房东身份和房子本身还是要自己核实。

## 多伦多租房app：找室友用什么？

室友平台重点在"人"，不只是"房"。刚来多伦多人生地不熟、想和朋友一起整租、或者很在意以后和谁共用厨房的话，室友 app 特别有用。挑平台时看几点：

- [ ] 是否按**生活习惯**匹配：作息、卫生、访客、抽烟、宠物，而不只看预算
- [ ] 是否对用户和房东有**某种核实**
- [ ] **隐私保护**：照片和个人信息是否默认公开
- [ ] 房源信息是否写明**房东是否同住**
- [ ] 能否**组队一起申请**

怎么挑到合拍的室友，可以看 [多伦多找室友指南](/zh/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/)。

## 51、约克论坛、小红书哪个靠谱？

这是华人租客问得最多的问题。老实说，三个渠道各有长处，靠不靠谱主要看你怎么用：

| 渠道 | 优点 | 常见风险 |
|---|---|---|
| 51.ca（加国无忧） | 分类信息多，老牌华人网站，房源覆盖大多伦多 | 帖子质量参差，有中介和二房东混在其中 |
| 约克论坛 (YorkBBS) | 华人常用的老牌论坛，租房、找室友帖子多 | 匿名发帖，需要自己核实身份 |
| 小红书 | 有图有视频，留学生多，能看到真实居住体验 | 假房源、盗图、开学前"代找房"骗定金 |
| 微信群 | 沟通最快，常有同校同乡推荐 | 群成员无法核实，冒充房东最常见 |

共同的防骗原则：视频确认对方本人，问清是房东、物业还是二房东；二房东分租要确认房东同意；不给没看过的房子转钱。每年8月和12月开学前，假房源明显增多，越着急越要慢下来。更多骗局套路和被骗后怎么办，详见 [多伦多租房防骗指南](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 按你的情况，这样搭配最省事

- **刚拿到录取、人还在国内的留学生**：学校校外住房平台 + 室友匹配平台，先找好室友再一起看房；中文渠道只用来了解行情，不要隔空转定金。
- **刚落地的新移民家庭**：Rentals.ca、Zumper 看整套公寓和 Condo，51.ca 看华人房东的独立屋和地下室，比较价格和通勤后再约看房。
- **在市中心上班、预算有限的上班族**：Kijiji、Facebook 找单间，室友平台找作息相近的人合租，签约前对照标准租约逐条确认。
- **想和朋友整租一套房**：优先找支持按房间分别申请或组队申请的平台，谁住哪间、各付多少，申请阶段就讲清楚。

## 不管用哪个网站，这五步都要做

1. **搜照片、搜地址**：用以图搜图查照片是否被盗用，看同一地址是否在别处以不同价格出租。
2. **核实身份**：问清房东的法定全名，和租约对照；Condo 要问对方是业主还是持牌中介。
3. **先看房再付钱**：实地看，或者实时视频，从街道、楼门口拍到房间门牌号。
4. **先签约后付款**：安省大多数住宅租赁使用标准租约，押金最多一个月房租。
5. **用可追踪的方式付款**：e-transfer 或支票，并索要收据。不要付现金、加密货币、礼品卡，也不要电汇给陌生人。

准备递交申请时，房东会要哪些材料，可以参考 [多伦多租房申请材料](/zh/blog/rental-application-toronto/)。

## 少踩坑，找到合适的家

## 常见问题

**多伦多哪个租房平台最不容易被骗？**
没有哪个平台能保证零诈骗。会核实房东或房源的平台、只接受注册房东的学校租房平台，相对多了一道把关；而开放的分类广告和社交媒体，任何人几分钟就能发帖。无论在哪找房，都要核实房东身份、实地或视频看房、签约前不付钱。

**人还在国内，怎么在多伦多找房？**
先用学校的校外住房平台 (off-campus housing)，再配合大型租房网站和室友平台。看房一定要实时视频，请对方从街道、楼门口一路拍到房间门牌。不要给任何没核实过的房源转定金，也可以先订短租，落地后再实地看房。

**在多伦多用租房网站要收费吗？**
大多数大型租房网站对租客浏览和联系房东是免费的，有的提供付费增值服务。如果有人要你先交钱才告诉地址或安排看房，要高度警惕。付费前请先看清平台自己的条款。

**在微信群里找到的房子，签约时要注意什么？**
先确认对方是房东本人、物业管理人，还是二房东；如果是二房东，问清房东是否同意分租。安省大多数住宅租赁要使用标准租约 (Ontario Standard Lease)，押金最多一个月房租，付款用可追踪的方式并索要收据。

# Bill 60 Ontario Tenants: What Changed in 2026

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/bill-60-ontario-tenants/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Bill 60 Ontario tenants guide, as of November 2026: the 7-day N4 notice, the 15-day LTB review deadline, the half-arrears rule and the new N12 rules.

Bill 60 gave Ontario tenants a new set of rules in 2026: as of November 2026, the notice period on an N4 for unpaid rent is 7 days instead of 14, you have 15 days instead of 30 to ask the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) to review an order, and tenants must pay half the claimed arrears before raising their own issues at a rent hearing. Together with parts of Bill 97, the changes took effect in two stages, on July 1 and September 21, 2026. Your basic protections are still there, though: a notice is not an eviction, and only an LTB order enforced by the Sheriff can make you leave.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the LTB, a community legal clinic or, in Toronto, 311.*

## Key takeaways

- **N4 notice period: 7 days** (down from 14) for notices given on or after September 21, 2026.
- **LTB review deadline: 15 days** (down from 30) for orders issued on or after July 1, 2026.
- **Half-arrears rule:** to raise maintenance or other issues at a rent-arrears hearing, you must pay the landlord at least half of the arrears claimed, at least 7 days before the hearing, for applications filed on or after September 21, 2026.
- **N12 change:** no compensation is owed for a landlord's own-use N12 that gives at least 120 days' notice and is served on or after September 21, 2026.
- **New forms:** the N4, N12 and N13 were replaced. Old versions may not be valid.

## What is Bill 60?

Bill 60, the *Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act, 2025*, is a provincial housing and infrastructure law that passed at Queen's Park in November 2025 amid protests from tenant groups. Among other things, it amended Ontario's *Residential Tenancies Act* (RTA), the law that governs most rentals. Some RTA changes from another law, Bill 97, were brought into force on the same schedule.

The government said the changes would speed up the LTB and encourage more rental housing. Tenant advocates, including the Advocacy Centre for Tenants Ontario, argued they make it faster and easier to evict people who fall behind. Either way, the rules are now law, so it pays to know them.

## Bill 60 Ontario tenants timeline

| Date | Change | What it means for you |
|---|---|---|
| July 1, 2026 | Review requests: 15 days, not 30 | Act fast if you disagree with an LTB order |
| July 1, 2026 | LTB Payment Agreement Form required for repayment plans under section 206 | Payment plans with your landlord must use the official form |
| July 1, 2026 | Air conditioner rules | You may install a window or portable unit under certain conditions; if electricity is included in rent, the landlord may charge a seasonal increase |
| July 1, 2026 | Higher maximum fines for RTA offences | Up to $100,000 for individuals and $500,000 for corporations |
| September 21, 2026 | N4 notice period: 7 days, not 14 | Less time to catch up before a landlord can file |
| September 21, 2026 | Half-arrears rule at rent hearings | Raising your own issues now costs money up front |
| September 21, 2026 | Own-use N12 with 120+ days' notice: no compensation | Plan for moving costs yourself |
| September 21, 2026 | New N4, N12 and N13 forms | Check the version date on any notice you get |

## N4 notice 7 days: what actually happens

An N4 is the form a landlord gives when rent is late. Since September 21, 2026, the termination date on a new N4 can be as early as 7 days after it's given, for monthly and yearly tenancies too.

That's tighter, but the steps that follow are the same:

1. **You get the N4.** It's a notice, not an order. You don't have to move.
2. **You can void it by paying.** Pay the full amount on the notice, plus any rent that has come due since, by the termination date, and the notice no longer counts. Keep proof of every payment.
3. **If arrears remain, the landlord can file an L1** application with the LTB.
4. **A hearing is scheduled.** You can still pay what's owed (including the landlord's filing fee) before an eviction order is issued, or ask for a payment plan.
5. **Only the Sheriff can enforce an eviction order.** Your landlord can never change the locks or remove your things on their own.

If you're struggling, talk to your landlord early and put any payment plan in writing. Our guide to [Ontario tenant rights](/blog/ontario-tenant-rights/) explains the wider protections you keep.

### The half-arrears rule

Before, a tenant facing an arrears hearing could raise problems like broken heat or harassment and ask the LTB to weigh them. You still can, but for applications filed on or after September 21, 2026, you must pay the landlord at least half of the claimed arrears at least 7 days before the hearing, and give written notice of the issues you want to raise. The payment goes to the landlord, not to the LTB in trust. If repairs are your main concern, filing your own application is often the stronger route; see how to file [LTB tenant applications](/blog/ltb-tenant-applications/).

## LTB review deadline 15 days

If the LTB issues an order you believe contains a serious error, such as a hearing you couldn't attend for a good reason, you can request a review. For orders issued on or after July 1, 2026, the deadline is 15 days from the order date, not 30. The LTB can extend it if it considers that just, but you should never count on that.

A practical tip: the day you receive any LTB order, read it, note the date, and call a legal clinic if you disagree. Two weeks goes quickly.

## Changes to N12 own-use evictions

An N12 is used when a landlord, a close family member or a buyer plans to move in. For a landlord's own-use N12 served on or after September 21, 2026, no one month's compensation is owed if the notice gives at least 120 days. Shorter notices still require compensation, and purchaser N12s always do.

There's a new safeguard too. If the person named on the notice doesn't move in within 60 days, the LTB presumes bad faith if you later file a T5 application. The landlord can try to rebut that, but the burden shifts in your favour.

## What hasn't changed

- **A notice is never an eviction.** Only an LTB order, enforced by the Sheriff, can remove you.
- **The rent increase guideline still applies** to most units first occupied before November 15, 2018 (2.1% for 2026).
- **Your notice to leave still works the usual way.** Tenants end a tenancy with an N9; see [ending a tenancy with an N9](/blog/ending-a-tenancy-n9/).
- **Landlords still need 24 hours' written notice** to enter for most reasons.

## A quick checklist if you get a notice

- Check the form's version date and the termination date.
- Confirm the amount owed against your own records.
- Pay, or arrange a written payment plan, before the termination date if you can.
- Open every letter from the LTB and note hearing and review dates.
- Get free advice from a community legal clinic or Tenant Duty Counsel.

## FAQ

**Can my landlord evict me 7 days after I miss rent?**
No. Seven days is only the minimum notice period on an N4 for notices given on or after September 21, 2026. If you don't pay, the landlord still has to file with the Landlord and Tenant Board, attend a hearing and get an eviction order, and only the Sheriff can enforce it.

**Does Bill 60 change rent control in Ontario?**
The tenancy changes now in force focus on notices, hearings, reviews and own-use evictions. The annual rent increase guideline still applies to most units first occupied before November 15, 2018, and it is 2.1% for 2026. Check ontario.ca for the current rules before a renewal.

**Do the new rules apply to notices I received before September 21, 2026?**
Generally not. The LTB says the 7-day N4 period applies to notices given on or after September 21, 2026, the half-arrears rule applies to applications filed on or after that date, and the N12 change applies to notices served on or after it. Older notices follow the earlier rules.

**Can I still get more time after an LTB order?**
You can ask, but the window to request a review of an order is now 15 days for orders issued on or after July 1, 2026, and the LTB only extends it when it considers that just. Tenant duty counsel or a community legal clinic can help you act quickly.

**Where can I get free help with Bill 60 changes?**
Contact your local community legal clinic through Legal Aid Ontario, Tenant Duty Counsel on the day of an LTB hearing, or the Advocacy Centre for Tenants Ontario's resources. In Toronto, call 311 to reach the City's Tenant Support Program.

## Sources

- [Tribunals Ontario: LTB operational update, legislative changes effective September 21, 2026](https://tribunalsontario.ca/2026/09/21/ltb-operational-update-legislative-changes-at-the-landlord-and-tenant-board-effective-september-21-2026/)
- [Tribunals Ontario: LTB operational update, legislative changes at the LTB (July 1, 2026)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/2026/06/30/ltb-operational-update-legislative-changes-at-the-ltb/)
- [Tribunals Ontario: What a landlord can do if a tenant does not pay rent (brochure)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/If%20a%20Tenant%20Does%20Not%20Pay%20Rent.html)
- [Government of Ontario: Residential Tenancies Act, 2006](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Advocacy Centre for Tenants Ontario: Top 5 concerns on Bill 60](https://www.acto.ca/actos-top-5-concerns-for-bill-60/)
- [Gowling WLG: Ontario's new LTB rules now in effect](https://gowlingwlg.com/en-ca/insights-resources/articles/2026/ontario-new-ltb-rules)
- [Government of Ontario: Residential rent increases](https://www.ontario.ca/page/residential-rent-increases)

# 安省Bill 60 租客新规：2026年改了什么

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/bill-60-ontario-tenants/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

安省Bill 60 租客新规详解（截至2026年11月）：欠租N4通知缩短为7天、LTB复审期限改为15天、欠租听证先付一半、N12自住驱逐新规，租客该怎么应对。

安省Bill 60 租客新规的核心是三件事：截至2026年11月，欠租时房东发的 N4 通知期限从14天缩短为7天；对房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 的裁决申请复审，期限从30天缩短为15天；欠租听证时如果你想提出维修等其他问题，要先付一半欠款。这些改动连同 Bill 97 的部分条款，分两批在2026年7月1日和9月21日生效。但最基本的保护没有变：收到通知不等于被驱逐，只有 LTB 驱逐令加上法警 (Sheriff) 执行，才能让你搬走。

*本文为一般性信息，不构成法律建议。具体情况请咨询 LTB、社区法律诊所，多伦多居民也可拨打311。*

## 先看重点

- **N4 欠租通知：7天**（原来14天），适用于2026年9月21日及之后发出的通知。
- **LTB 复审期限：15天**（原来30天），适用于2026年7月1日及之后发出的裁决。
- **欠租听证"先付一半"**：2026年9月21日及之后提交的欠租申请，租客想在听证上提出自己的问题，必须在听证至少7天前把所欠金额的一半付给房东。
- **N12 自住驱逐**：2026年9月21日及之后送达、提前至少120天通知的房东自住 N12，不再需要给一个月房租补偿。
- **表格更新**：N4、N12、N13 都换了新版，旧版本可能无效。

## 安省Bill 60 租客新规是什么？

Bill 60 全称《加快建设、减少拖延法案》(Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act, 2025)，是安省政府的住房和基建法案，2025年11月在省议会通过，当时租客团体在场外抗议。法案修改了安省《住宅租赁法》(Residential Tenancies Act，简称 RTA)，也就是规管大多数租房关系的法律；另一部法律 Bill 97 中的部分条款也按同一时间表生效。

政府的说法是：这些改动能加快 LTB 处理速度，鼓励更多出租房源。安省租客倡导中心 (ACTO) 等团体则认为，新规让欠租的租客更快、更容易被驱逐。不管立场如何，新规已经是法律，租客必须了解。

## 2026租客新规有哪些？一张表看懂

| 生效日期 | 改了什么 | 对租客意味着什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 2026年7月1日 | 申请复审期限改为15天 | 对 LTB 裁决有异议要尽快行动 |
| 2026年7月1日 | 按 RTA 第206条达成的还款协议必须使用 LTB 官方表格 | 和房东谈分期补交，要用正式表格 |
| 2026年7月1日 | 空调新规 | 符合条件时租客可以装窗式或移动空调；如果房租包电费，房东可以收季节性附加费 |
| 2026年7月1日 | 违反 RTA 的最高罚款提高 | 个人最高10万加元，公司最高50万加元 |
| 2026年9月21日 | N4 通知期限改为7天 | 补交欠款的缓冲时间变短 |
| 2026年9月21日 | 欠租听证"先付一半" | 想在听证上提维修等问题，要先拿出钱 |
| 2026年9月21日 | 提前120天以上的房东自住 N12 无需补偿 | 搬家费可能要自己承担 |
| 2026年9月21日 | N4、N12、N13 换新版 | 收到通知先看表格版本日期 |

## 欠租7天就被通知？N4 新规到底怎么走

N4 是房东在租客迟交房租时发出的"欠租终止租约通知"。2026年9月21日起，新发出的 N4 上写的终止日期，最早可以是通知发出后第7天，按月交租、按年交租的租约也一样。

时间紧了，但后面的流程没有变：

1. **收到 N4**：这只是通知，不是命令，你不需要立刻搬走。
2. **补交即可作废**：在通知上的终止日期前，把通知上的欠款加上之后到期的房租全部付清，这份 N4 就失效了。每一笔付款都要留好凭证（转账记录、收据）。
3. **仍有欠款，房东可以向 LTB 提交 L1 申请**。
4. **LTB 安排听证**：在驱逐令发出前，你仍然可以付清欠款和房东的申请费，或者申请分期还款。
5. **只有法警能执行驱逐令**：房东自己换锁、扔东西都是违法的。

刚落地的新移民、等奖学金或家里汇款的留学生，最容易遇到"钱晚几天到账"的情况。建议提前和房东沟通，把分期补交的安排写成书面文字。更多基本权利可以看 [安省租客权益](/zh/blog/ontario-tenant-rights/)。

### 欠租听证"先付一半"是什么意思？

以前，租客在欠租听证上可以提出房子暖气坏了、房东骚扰等问题，请 LTB 一并考虑。现在仍然可以，但对2026年9月21日及之后提交的申请，你必须在听证至少7天前把房东主张的欠款至少一半付给房东（不是交给 LTB 托管），同时以书面形式说明你要提出的问题。如果你最主要的诉求是维修，自己单独向 LTB 提交租客申请（比如 T6 维修申请）往往更稳妥。

## LTB 复审期限缩短为15天

如果你认为 LTB 的裁决有严重错误，比如你因正当理由没能参加听证，可以申请复审 (review)。2026年7月1日及之后发出的裁决，申请期限是裁决日期起15天，不再是30天。LTB 在认为合理时可以延长，但千万不要指望这一点。

实用建议：收到任何 LTB 文件当天就打开看，记下日期；看不懂英文就马上找人帮忙翻译，或联系社区法律诊所。两周时间过得非常快。

## N12 房东自住驱逐有什么变化？

N12 用于房东本人、近亲属或买家要搬进来住的情况。2026年9月21日及之后送达的房东自住 N12，如果提前至少120天通知，就不用再给一个月房租补偿；通知期不足120天的，仍然要补偿；买家自住的 N12 无论如何都要补偿。

同时也多了一条保护：如果通知上写的人在60天内没有搬进来，你之后向 LTB 提交 T5（恶意驱逐）申请时，LTB 会推定房东是恶意的，由房东来反驳。这对租客维权更有利。

## 合租、和房东同住，新规适用吗？

很多留学生和新移民租的是独立屋里的一个房间，这时要先弄清楚自己是不是受 RTA 保护的"租客"：

- **和房东本人（或房东的父母、子女等近亲）共用厨房或卫生间**：通常不受 RTA 管辖，也就谈不上 N4、LTB 听证这些程序，Bill 60 的新规同样不适用。纠纷一般只能通过协商或小额索偿法庭 (Small Claims Court) 解决，保护明显更少。
- **房东不住在里面，几个租客各自和房东签约**：一般受 RTA 保护，新规适用。
- **几个人一起签一份租约**：大家都是共同租客，一个人欠租，整份租约都可能收到 N4。

所以看房时一定要问清楚：房东住不住在这里？厨房、卫生间和谁共用？租约上写的是谁的名字？

## 哪些规则没有变？

- **通知不等于驱逐**：只有 LTB 驱逐令加法警执行才能让你搬走。
- **涨租指导线照常适用**：2018年11月15日之前首次入住的大多数单位，2026年续租涨幅上限为2.1%。
- **租客主动退租**仍然使用 N9 表格，具体看 [安省退租 N9](/zh/blog/ending-a-tenancy-n9/)。
- **房东进屋**一般仍需提前24小时书面通知。
- **租约格式**：大多数住宅租赁仍须使用 [安省标准租约](/zh/blog/ontario-standard-lease/)。

## 收到通知怎么办：租客自查清单

- 看清表格的版本日期和终止日期；
- 核对房东写的欠款金额和你自己的付款记录；
- 能补交就在终止日期前补交，或签书面分期协议；
- LTB 寄来的每一封信都要拆开，记下听证和复审日期；
- 尽早联系社区法律诊所或租客值班律师，不要拖到最后一天。

## 常见问题

**欠租7天房东就能把我赶走吗？**
不能。7天只是2026年9月21日及之后发出的 N4 通知的最短期限。如果你没有补交，房东还必须向房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 申请、参加听证并拿到驱逐令，最后只有法警 (Sheriff) 才能执行。

**Bill 60 改变了涨租上限吗？**
目前生效的租赁改动主要集中在通知、听证、复审和自住驱逐上。2018年11月15日之前首次入住的大多数单位，续租涨幅仍受安省指导线限制，2026年为2.1%。续租前可以在安省政府网站确认最新规定。

**我在9月21日之前收到的通知按新规还是旧规？**
一般按旧规。LTB 说明：7天 N4 期限适用于2026年9月21日及之后发出的通知；欠租听证先付一半适用于当天及之后提交的申请；N12 新规适用于当天及之后送达的通知。之前的通知仍按原来的规则处理。

**对 LTB 的裁决不服，还来得及申请复审吗？**
2026年7月1日及之后发出的裁决，申请复审的期限是15天，以前是30天。LTB 只有在认为合理时才会延长期限，所以收到裁决当天就要看清日期，尽快联系社区法律诊所。

**华人租客去哪里找免费的法律帮助？**
可以通过安省法律援助 (Legal Aid Ontario) 找到所在区域的社区法律诊所，LTB 听证当天也有租客值班律师 (Tenant Duty Counsel)。多伦多居民可以拨打311，联系市政府的租客支援项目，部分服务提供中文协助。

## 参考资料

- [Tribunals Ontario：LTB 运营更新，2026年9月21日生效的法律修改](https://tribunalsontario.ca/2026/09/21/ltb-operational-update-legislative-changes-at-the-landlord-and-tenant-board-effective-september-21-2026/)
- [Tribunals Ontario：LTB 运营更新，2026年7月1日生效的法律修改](https://tribunalsontario.ca/2026/06/30/ltb-operational-update-legislative-changes-at-the-ltb/)
- [Tribunals Ontario：租客不交房租时房东可以做什么（宣传册）](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/If%20a%20Tenant%20Does%20Not%20Pay%20Rent.html)
- [安省政府：Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（住宅租赁法）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)

# Brampton Rental Licence: What Tenants Should Check

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/brampton-rental-licensing/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Brampton rental licence rules as of November 2026: now citywide. How to check if your rental is licensed, basement apartment rules, fines and Caledon's program.

A Brampton rental licence is now required citywide: as of November 2026, every owner renting out a property with one to four units anywhere in Brampton needs a Residential Rental Licence from the City before advertising, collecting rent or letting anyone move in. The program expanded from five central wards to all ten on January 1, 2026, and runs as a pilot until December 31, 2028. For tenants, the licence is a quick, free way to check that a home has been on the City's radar for safety.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For questions about your tenancy, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic; for licensing, call Brampton 311.*

## Key takeaways

- **Citywide since January 1, 2026:** wards 2, 6, 8, 9 and 10 joined wards 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7.
- **Who needs it:** owners renting properties with one to four residential units, including owner-occupied homes with a rented basement or other additional unit.
- **Free to apply** as of the City's December 2025 announcement; licences are renewed every year and don't transfer to a new owner.
- **Escalating fines** for renting without a licence: $750, then $1,250, then $1,500 for later offences.
- **Basements must be registered** with the City as additional residential units, and the City publishes a list and map of registered units.
- **Caledon** launched its own licensing in September 2026, starting with short-term rentals.

## How Brampton rental licence rules work

Brampton started its Residential Rental Licensing (RRL) pilot in January 2024 in five central wards, to tackle unsafe and overcrowded rentals. In December 2025, following a deadly fire at a rental home, Council expanded it citywide and added tougher fines.

Under the program, an owner must hold a licence before:

- advertising a unit for rent,
- collecting rent, or
- letting a tenant move in.

The licence must be displayed in a visible spot inside the rental, and the licence number should appear on ads and on documents like leases and receipts. Owners must renew every year, and a buyer has to apply for a new licence after a sale.

**Not covered:** licensed lodging houses (they fall under separate business licensing) and larger buildings with five or more units.

## Is my rental licensed in Brampton?

A few minutes of checking before you sign can save you a lot of trouble.

### Your pre-lease checklist

- **Ask for the licence number** in writing. A legitimate landlord should have it ready.
- **Look for it on the ad.** No number on a Brampton listing is a reason to ask questions.
- **Check the licence on site.** It should be posted inside the unit.
- **For a basement or second unit, search the City's registered units list** by address.
- **Confirm with the City.** If the landlord's answer is vague, contact Brampton 311.
- **Look for the basics:** working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, clear exits and no blocked-off windows or hallways.

A missing licence doesn't automatically mean a scam, but combined with pressure to pay a deposit quickly or a refusal to show the unit, it's a serious red flag. Our guide to [rental scams in Toronto](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) covers the warning signs that apply across the GTA.

## Brampton basement apartment rules

Basements are where most of Brampton's rental questions come up. Here's what tenants should know:

- **Registration:** to be legal, a second unit, third unit or garden suite must be registered with the City of Brampton. Registration involves permits and inspections.
- **Licensing:** a rented additional unit also needs a Residential Rental Licence, even when the owner lives upstairs.
- **Check the list:** the City publishes a map and a list of registered two-unit and three-unit dwellings and garden suites.
- **Safety first:** a legal basement unit should have proper exits, adequate windows, working alarms and fire separation from the main house.

If the owner lives in the house and you share a kitchen or bathroom with them, the *Residential Tenancies Act* usually doesn't apply, which means fewer protections. A self-contained basement with its own kitchen and bathroom is different. For a full rundown of what makes a basement legal and safe, read our pillar guide to [legal basement apartments](/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/).

## Shared houses and students in Brampton

Brampton is home to Sheridan College's Davis campus and Algoma University's Brampton campus, and many international students share houses. City guidance says rooms can be rented without a lodging house licence to up to four lodgers, in up to four bedrooms per dwelling unit. A home renting rooms to more people than that generally needs a lodging house licence.

| Setup | What usually applies |
|---|---|
| Whole house rented to one group on one lease | Residential Rental Licence (1–4 units) |
| Up to 4 bedrooms rented to up to 4 lodgers per unit | No lodging house licence needed; ask whether the property also holds an RRL |
| More than 4 lodgers renting separate rooms | Lodging house licence under business licensing |
| Basement unit rented separately | Registered additional unit plus Residential Rental Licence |

Signs of trouble include bunk beds in living rooms, padlocks on every door, or more than one person per bedroom without your agreement. New to renting in Canada? Our guide to [international student housing in Toronto](/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/) explains leases, deposits and your rights.

## What if your rental isn't licensed?

Finding out your landlord has no licence can be unsettling, but it doesn't put you in trouble. The fines are aimed at owners, not tenants. A few sensible steps:

- **Keep paying rent** and keep proof of every payment. Withholding rent can give the landlord grounds for an N4.
- **Ask the landlord, in writing,** whether they've applied for a licence and when they expect it.
- **Report safety problems right away** through Brampton 311, especially missing alarms, blocked exits or overcrowding.
- **Get advice before you move out.** A community legal clinic can tell you how your lease and the *Residential Tenancies Act* apply.
- **Write everything down:** dates, photos and messages make any later complaint much stronger.

## Caledon rental licensing

Just north of Brampton, the Town of Caledon launched its own Residential Rental Licensing program on September 8, 2026, citing overcrowding, illegal units and poor maintenance. It's rolling out in phases:

- **Short-term rentals** (like Airbnb) needed a licence from launch.
- **Long-term rentals** are scheduled to follow in 2027.
- **Fees:** an introductory $250 until November 6, 2026, then $500.

If you're considering a long-term rental in Caledon, ask the landlord whether they plan to license once the long-term phase begins.

## Find a safer shared home

## FAQ

**Do I lose my tenant rights if my Brampton landlord isn't licensed?**
Generally no. The licence is the landlord's obligation, and the Residential Tenancies Act protects most tenants whether or not the landlord follows City rules. If your unit is unsafe or unlicensed, you can report it to the City through 311 and get advice from a community legal clinic.

**Does a Brampton rental licence cost tenants anything?**
No. The licence is applied for and held by the property owner, and the City said in December 2025 that new and renewal applications would remain free. A landlord shouldn't pass a licence fee on to you as a separate charge.

**Can international students share a house in Brampton legally?**
Yes, if it's set up properly. City guidance allows rooms to be rented to up to four lodgers in up to four bedrooms per dwelling unit without a lodging house licence; more than that generally needs a lodging house licence. Rented basement units must also be registered and licensed.

**How do I report an illegal rental in Brampton?**
Contact Brampton 311 and give the address and what you've seen, such as overcrowding, no smoke alarms or no visible licence. If it's an emergency, such as fire or no exit, call 911 first.

**Do long-term rentals in Caledon need a licence yet?**
Not yet, as of November 2026. Caledon's program started with short-term rentals on September 8, 2026, and the Town says long-term rentals will follow in 2027. Check the Town's rental licence page before you sign a lease there.

## Sources

- [City of Brampton: Residential Rental Licensing FAQs](https://www.brampton.ca/EN/Business/Licensing/Residential-Rental-Licensing/Pages/FAQS.aspx)
- [City of Brampton news release: Residential Rental Licensing expands city-wide, new escalating fines (December 2025)](https://www.brampton.ca/EN/City-Hall/News/Pages/News-Release.aspx/1621)
- [City of Brampton: Registered Additional Residential Units (map and list)](https://www.brampton.ca/EN/residents/Building-Permits/second-dwelling/Pages/Registered-Additional-Residential-Units.aspx)
- [City of Brampton: Shared accommodations and lodging houses](https://www.brampton.ca/EN/residents/Renting/Pages/Shared-Accommodations.aspx)
- [Town of Caledon: Town launches Residential Rental Licensing program](https://www.caledon.ca/en/news/town-of-caledon-launches-residential-rental-licensing-program.aspx)
- [Town of Caledon: Rental Licence Program](https://www.caledon.ca/en/town-services/rental-license-program.aspx)

# 宾顿出租屋执照：租客入住前要查什么

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/brampton-rental-licensing/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

宾顿出租屋执照2026年起全市强制（截至2026年11月）：怎么查房东有没有执照、宾顿地下室租房合法吗、学生合租几人算合规、无照罚款多少，以及卡利登新规。

宾顿出租屋执照现在全市强制：截至2026年11月，在宾顿 (Brampton) 任何一个区出租一到四个住宅单位的业主，都必须先向市政府领取"住宅出租执照"(Residential Rental Licence)，才能打广告、收房租或让租客入住。这个项目在2026年1月1日从市中心五个选区扩大到全部十个选区，试点期一直到2028年12月31日。对租客来说，执照是一个免费又快速的办法，可以判断这套房子有没有进入市政府的安全监管视线。

*本文为一般性信息，不构成法律建议。租约问题可咨询房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律诊所；执照问题请联系宾顿311。*

## 先看重点

- **2026年1月1日起全市实施**：2、6、8、9、10区加入原来的1、3、4、5、7区。
- **谁需要执照**：出租一到四个住宅单位的业主，包括自住、只把地下室或附加单位租出去的房主。
- **申请免费**（据市政府2025年12月公告），每年续期，房子卖掉后新业主要重新申请。
- **无照出租罚款逐级加重**：第一次750加元，第二次1,250加元，之后每次1,500加元。
- **地下室必须登记**为附加住宅单位，市政府公开了已登记单位的名单和地图。
- **卡利登** (Caledon) 2026年9月推出自己的出租执照，先从短租开始。

## 宾顿出租屋执照是怎么回事？

宾顿从2024年1月开始在市中心五个选区试行住宅出租执照 (RRL)，目的是整治不安全、过度拥挤的出租屋。2025年12月，在一起出租屋致命火灾之后，市议会决定把项目扩大到全市，并提高罚款。

按规定，业主必须先拿到执照，才可以：

- 发布出租广告；
- 收取房租；
- 让租客搬进来。

执照要张贴在出租单位内显眼的位置，执照号码应该出现在广告以及租约、收据等文件上。执照每年续期，不能转让。

**不在范围内的**：另有商业执照管理的寄宿屋 (lodging house)，以及五个单位以上的较大楼宇。

对租客来说，执照的意义在于：业主申请时要向市政府申报房屋的卧室、厨房、卫生间等情况，市政府也可能上门检查是否符合建筑、消防和物业标准。换句话说，有执照的房子至少被"看过一眼"，比完全没人管的出租屋多一层保障。

## 怎么查房东有没有执照？

签约前花几分钟核实，能省下很多麻烦。

### 签约前自查清单

- **书面向房东要执照号码**，正规房东应该随时能提供；
- **看广告上有没有执照号**，宾顿的房源没写号码，就要多问几句；
- **看房时找执照**，应该张贴在屋内；
- **地下室或第二单位，用地址在市政府的已登记单位名单里搜索**；
- **向市政府确认**，房东说不清楚的话，直接联系宾顿311；
- **检查基本安全**：烟雾报警器和一氧化碳报警器能用，出口通畅，窗户和走廊没有被堵住。

没有执照不一定就是骗局，但如果再加上催你快交定金、不让实地看房，就是非常明显的危险信号。微信群、小红书上的宾顿租房帖尤其要留心，更多识别方法见 [多伦多租房诈骗](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 宾顿地下室租房合法吗？

宾顿很多出租房是地下室，合不合法主要看两点：

- **是否登记**：第二单位、第三单位或花园套房 (garden suite) 必须在宾顿市政府登记才算合法，登记需要经过许可和检查。
- **是否有出租执照**：单独出租的附加单位还需要住宅出租执照，即使房主本人住在楼上也一样。

市政府公布了已登记的两单位、三单位住宅和花园套房的地图和名单，签约前可以按地址查一查。合法的地下室应该有合格的出口和窗户、能用的报警器，以及和主屋之间的防火分隔。

还要注意：如果房主住在屋里，你和房主共用厨房或卫生间，通常不受 RTA 保护，权益少很多；有独立厨房和卫生间的地下室套房则不同。地下室怎样才算合法安全，详见 [多伦多地下室租房](/zh/blog/legal-basement-apartments-toronto/)。

## 宾顿学生合租：几个人算合规？

宾顿有谢尔丹学院 (Sheridan College) 的 Davis 校区和阿尔戈马大学 (Algoma University) 宾顿校区，很多国际学生选择合租独立屋。根据市政府的说明，每个住宅单位最多可以把不超过四间卧室分租给不超过四名寄宿者，不需要寄宿屋执照；超过这个人数，一般就需要寄宿屋执照。

| 情况 | 一般适用的规定 |
|---|---|
| 整栋房子租给一群人，签一份租约 | 住宅出租执照（1到4个单位） |
| 每个单位分租不超过4间卧室、不超过4人 | 不需要寄宿屋执照，可问房东是否持有出租执照 |
| 超过4人各自租单间 | 需要按商业执照规定申请寄宿屋执照 |
| 地下室单独出租 | 登记附加单位，加上住宅出租执照 |

客厅摆满上下铺、每个房门都上锁、一间卧室未经你同意塞进两三个人，这些都是危险信号。第一次在加拿大租房的同学，可以先看 [多伦多留学生租房](/zh/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/)，了解租约、押金和基本权利。

## 在宾顿看房，可以直接问房东这几句

很多人不好意思开口，其实这些问题都很正常，正规房东不会介意：

- "这套房子的出租执照号码是多少？方便拍照给我吗？"
- "地下室在市政府登记过吗？是两单位住宅 (two-unit dwelling) 吗？"
- "这一层一共住几个人？厨房和卫生间几个人共用？"
- "房东本人住在这里吗？"（关系到你是否受 RTA 保护）
- "用的是安省标准租约吗？房租怎么付，会给收据吗？"
- "水电、暖气、网络包不包？冬天暖气由谁控制？"

如果对方回答含糊、催你当天交钱，或者说"执照在办，先住进来再说"，最好再多看几家。宾顿房源不少，不必在一套有疑问的房子上冒险。

## 发现房子没有执照怎么办？

发现房东没有执照，难免心里打鼓，但罚款针对的是业主，不是租客。建议这样做：

- **照常交房租**并保留每一笔付款记录，私自停交房租可能让房东有理由发 N4 通知；
- **书面询问房东**是否已经申请执照、预计什么时候拿到；
- **安全问题立刻举报**，特别是没有报警器、出口被堵、人数过多，可通过宾顿311反映；
- **搬走之前先咨询**，社区法律诊所可以告诉你租约和 RTA 在你的情况下怎么适用；
- **把一切记录下来**：日期、照片、聊天记录，日后投诉会更有力。

## 卡利登出租执照

宾顿北边的卡利登镇 (Caledon) 于2026年9月8日推出了自己的住宅出租执照项目，理由是要解决过度拥挤、违规单位和维护不善等问题。项目分阶段实施：

- **短租**（如 Airbnb）从推出之日起就需要执照；
- **长租**计划在2027年纳入；
- **费用**：2026年11月6日前为优惠价250加元，之后为500加元。

如果你考虑在卡利登长租，可以问问房东，等长租阶段开始后是否打算申请执照。

## 找一个更安全的合租房

## 常见问题

**房东没有执照，我的租客权利还在吗？**
一般仍然在。执照是房东的义务，安省《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 对大多数租客的保护，并不取决于房东有没有遵守市政规定。如果房子不安全或没有执照，可以通过宾顿311向市政府举报，并向社区法律诊所咨询。

**宾顿出租执照要租客出钱吗？**
不用。执照由业主申请和持有，宾顿市政府在2025年12月表示新申请和续期仍然免费。房东不应该把"执照费"作为额外费用转嫁给租客。

**怎么举报宾顿的违规出租屋？**
联系宾顿311，提供地址和你看到的情况，比如人数过多、没有烟雾报警器、看不到执照等。如果是火灾、没有出口等紧急情况，先打911。

**卡利登的长租房现在需要执照吗？**
截至2026年11月还不需要。卡利登 (Caledon) 的出租执照项目于2026年9月8日先从短租开始，镇政府表示长租将在2027年纳入。在那边签长租约前，可以先看镇政府的出租执照页面。

**宾顿房东要求现金交租、不给收据正常吗？**
不正常，也要警惕。宾顿要求房东在租约、收据等文件上注明执照号码。坚持只收现金、不给收据、拿不出执照号码，往往说明房子可能没登记，你的押金和权益也更难保障。

## 参考资料

# Female Roommates Toronto: Women-Only Rooms and Safety

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/female-roommates-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Looking for female roommates in Toronto? When a women-only room is legal under Ontario's Human Rights Code, plus safety tips for meeting roommates and viewings.

Looking for female roommates in Toronto is common and, in many situations, perfectly legal. Ontario's Human Rights Code generally prohibits sex discrimination in housing, but it makes room for women-only homes in specific cases: when you'd share a kitchen or bathroom with a live-in owner or their family, or when **all** the accommodation in a building (other than the owner's family's) is limited to people of the same sex.

Below: what the law actually says, how to word a listing, and the safety habits that make meeting strangers a lot less nerve-racking.

## Key takeaways

- **The default rule:** housing can't be offered on discriminatory terms, including because of sex.
- **Exception 1, s. 21(1):** sharing a kitchen or bathroom with a live-in owner or their family.
- **Exception 2, s. 21(2):** a building where everyone, apart from the owner's family, is the same sex.
- **The same-sex exception covers sex only.** It doesn't permit other preferences, such as religion or ethnicity.
- **Safety first:** video call, meet in public, verify identity, view in daylight and never pay before seeing the room.

*This is general information, not legal advice. For questions about your rights, contact the Human Rights Legal Support Centre or a community legal clinic; for tenancy issues, the Landlord and Tenant Board.*

## Are women-only rooms legal in Ontario?

Section 2 of the Human Rights Code gives everyone the right to equal treatment in occupying housing, without discrimination because of grounds that include sex. Section 21 then sets out exceptions. Here's how they apply in real life:

| Situation | Can it be women-only? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Room in a house where you share the kitchen or bathroom with the owner or their family, who live there | Generally yes | s. 21(1) shared-accommodation exception |
| Whole house rented room by room, every room limited to women | Generally yes | s. 21(2): all accommodation in the building restricted to the same sex |
| Owner lives in the house, and every other room is rented to women | Generally yes | s. 21(2) excludes the owner's family's own space from the count |
| One room in a unit inside a large mixed apartment or condo building | Unclear | s. 21(2) refers to all the accommodation in the building; get advice |
| Self-contained apartment rented to a single tenant | Generally no | No exception applies; a sex-based refusal can be discrimination |

### The fine print that trips people up

- **"Sex only" means sex only.** The Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC) describes s. 21(2) as an exception for the ground of sex. It doesn't let a listing add "Chinese only," "Christian only" or "no international students." Only the broader s. 21(1) live-in-owner exemption reaches further.
- **Live-in owners and the RTA.** The s. 21(1) situation usually lines up with section 5(i) of the Residential Tenancies Act, which means the RTA often doesn't apply either. Read our guide to [living with your landlord](/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/) before you rent that kind of room.
- **Harassment rules are separate.** The Code also addresses sexual harassment in housing by a landlord, their agent or another occupant of the building (section 7). A women-only listing is about who gets the room; harassment protections are about how you're treated once you live there.

### Wording a listing

If an exception clearly fits, describe the household plainly and stick to facts: "women-only household, four bedrooms, two shared bathrooms." Skip extra preferences that aren't about sex. If you're a tenant searching for a roommate in a unit inside a bigger building, consider phrasing it as information about the household ("currently two women live here") and asking the OHRC's resources or a legal clinic if you're unsure.

### Women-only or women-friendly?

Not every woman needs a legally women-only home. Many are happy in a mixed household that's respectful and well run: clear guest rules, locks on bedroom doors, and roommates whose habits and schedules fit. Before you narrow your search to "women only," decide what actually makes you feel safe. Often it's the people, the building and the written agreement, more than the label on the listing.

## Female roommates Toronto: where to look

Women find roommates in the same places everyone does: school housing boards, workplace and community groups, Facebook groups, Kijiji and roommate apps. Our main guide on how to [find a roommate in Toronto](/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/) walks through the full process. What changes is the screening, because a fake profile can claim to be anyone.

## A safe roommate search for women

### Before you meet

- **Move the conversation to a video call.** A real person can show their face and the room live. Refusing to video call is a reason to stop.
- **Check the details line up.** Name, school or job, and photos should be consistent across their profile and messages.
- **Ask who else lives there and who visits.** Partners who are "basically always over" change the household.
- **Look up the address.** Make sure it's a real residential building and that the listing photos match the street view.

### At the viewing

- **Go in daylight, and bring a friend** or share your live location with someone.
- **Meet the actual roommates**, not just the person renting the room.
- **Check the bedroom door locks** and that the entrance, hallways and building feel secure.
- **Trust your instincts.** Pressure to decide on the spot, or to come alone at night, is a reason to leave.

### Before you pay

- **Never send money before seeing the room** and signing a written agreement.
- **Confirm the person can rent it to you.** Ask to see the lease, or confirm you're dealing with the owner or a verified agent.
- **Use traceable payment** such as e-transfer, and get a receipt for every payment.

Scammers often target women-only listings because demand is high and people feel pressure to grab a "safe" room fast. Our guides to [roommate red flags](/blog/roommate-red-flags/) and [rental scams in Toronto](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) cover the common scripts.

## Safety checklist for move-in day

- [ ] Written roommate agreement signed, including guest and overnight rules
- [ ] Copy of the lease, or the host's agreement, saved somewhere safe
- [ ] Emergency contact shared with a friend or family member
- [ ] Your own key, and the bedroom lock works
- [ ] Notes on who to contact for building issues (landlord, property manager, superintendent)

## Find roommates you feel safe with

## FAQ

**What should I do if a roommate or landlord sexually harasses me?**
If you're in danger, call 911. The Human Rights Code also has rules against sexual harassment in housing, including by a landlord, their agent or another occupant of the building. Keep messages and notes of what happened, and contact the Human Rights Legal Support Centre or a community legal clinic about your options.

**Is it okay to ask a potential roommate for ID?**
Yes, it's reasonable for both of you to confirm you are who you say you are, for example by showing photo ID on a video call or at the viewing. Share only what's needed: a name and photo match is enough. Never send your SIN, passport scans or banking details to someone you haven't met.

**Does a women-only household mean no male guests?**
Not automatically. Who rents the rooms and who can visit are separate questions. Agree on guest and overnight rules as a household and write them into your roommate agreement so nobody is surprised later.

**Is a women-only room automatically safer?**
No. A women-only label tells you who rents the rooms, not who the people are. Scammers know these listings are in demand, so screen the host and roommates just as carefully, and walk away from anyone who pressures you to pay before a viewing.

**What if a 'female only' listing turns out to be run by a man I can't meet?**
Treat any mismatch between the listing and the person you're dealing with as a warning sign. Ask for a video call with the actual roommates and proof the host can rent the room. If the story keeps changing, stop and report the listing to the platform.

## Sources

- [Human Rights Code, R.S.O. 1990 (sections 2, 7 and 21)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90h19)
- [OHRC: Policy on human rights and rental housing, III. The Ontario Human Rights Code](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/policy-human-rights-and-rental-housing/iii-ontario-human-rights-code)
- [OHRC: Rental housing and the Ontario Human Rights Code](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/book/export/html/3236)
- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (section 5)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Human Rights Legal Support Centre](https://www.hrlsc.on.ca/)

# 多伦多找女室友：只租女生合法吗？安全指南

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/female-roommates-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

多伦多找女室友，"只租女生"合法吗？按安省人权法第21条讲清哪些情况可以限女生、怎样写帖子，以及刚来多伦多的女生见室友、看房、付款和入住时的安全清单。

多伦多找女室友非常普遍，而且在很多情况下完全合法。安省人权法（Human Rights Code）原则上禁止住房方面的性别歧视，但对两种情况留了例外：一是你要和住在房子里的房东或其家人共用厨房或卫生间；二是一栋楼里（房东一家自住的部分除外）**所有**住处都只租给同一性别的人。

在小红书、微信群里，"限女生""女生合租""求女室友"的帖子每天都有。很多女生第一次出国、第一次和陌生人合住，最担心的就是住得安不安全，又怕自己写"只租女生"会不会违法。这篇先讲清法律上什么时候可以"只租女生"，再给一份实用的安全清单。

## 要点速览

- **基本原则**：出租住房不能带有歧视性条件，其中包括性别。
- **例外一，第21(1)条**：和同住的房东或其家人共用厨房或卫生间。
- **例外二，第21(2)条**：整栋楼除房东一家外，所有住户都是同一性别。
- **同性别例外只管性别**，不允许再加上宗教、族裔等其他偏好。
- **安全第一**：先视频、在公共场所见面、核实身份、白天看房，没看房绝不付钱。

*本文为一般信息，不构成法律意见。关于人权问题，可联系人权法律支援中心或社区法律诊所；租务问题可联系房东租客委员会（LTB）。*

## 只租女生合法吗？

人权法第2条规定，每个人在住房的居住方面都享有平等待遇，不因性别等理由受到歧视。第21条再列出例外。放到日常租房场景里，大致是这样：

| 情况 | 可以只租女生吗？ | 原因 |
|---|---|---|
| 房东或其家人住在家里，你要和他们共用厨房或卫生间 | 一般可以 | 第21(1)条共住例外 |
| 整栋house按房间出租，每个房间都只租女生 | 一般可以 | 第21(2)条：整栋楼都限同一性别 |
| 房东自住，其余房间全部租给女生 | 一般可以 | 第21(2)条不把房东一家自住的部分算在内 |
| 大型公寓楼或condo里某个单元中的一个房间 | 不明确 | 第21(2)条说的是"整栋楼"的所有住处，最好咨询 |
| 整套独立公寓租给一个租客 | 一般不可以 | 没有适用的例外，按性别拒租可能构成歧视 |

### 容易被忽略的细节

- **"只管性别"就是只管性别**。安省人权委员会（OHRC）把第21(2)条描述为针对性别这一项的例外。帖子里不能借此再加上"只租华人""只租基督徒""不租留学生"。只有范围更广的第21(1)条（与同住房东共用厨卫）才不止于此。
- **和房东同住，RTA也可能不适用**。第21(1)条的情况通常也符合住宅租赁法（Residential Tenancies Act, RTA）第5(i)条，也就是说RTA往往不保护你。租这类房间前，建议先看[和房东同住指南](/zh/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/)。
- **防骚扰是另一套规则**。人权法第7条也处理住房中的性骚扰，包括来自房东、房东代理人或同楼其他住户的骚扰。"限女生"决定的是谁能租到房间，防骚扰保护的是你住进去以后如何被对待。

### 帖子怎么写

如果明显符合例外，就平实地描述这个家："全女生合租，四个卧室，两个共用卫生间"，不要再附加和性别无关的要求。如果你是租客，在一栋大楼里的某个单元找室友，可以写成对现状的描述，比如"目前住着两个女生"；拿不准的话，看看OHRC的资料或问问法律诊所。

### 一定要"只租女生"吗？

不是每个女生都需要法律意义上的"女生专属"房子。很多人住在男女混合的合租屋里也很舒服，关键是这个家管理得好：访客规则清楚、卧室门能上锁、室友的作息和习惯合得来。缩小范围之前，先想清楚到底是什么让你有安全感。很多时候，真正起作用的是人、楼和书面协议，而不是帖子上的标签。

## 多伦多找女室友：去哪里找

女生找室友的渠道和大家一样：学校住房平台、公司或社区群、Facebook群、Kijiji、室友App，还有华人常用的微信群、小红书、51.ca、约克论坛。完整的找室友流程可以看[多伦多找室友指南](/zh/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/)。不同的是筛选要更严，因为假账号可以自称任何人。

## 女生找室友的安全清单

### 见面之前

- **先视频通话**。真人可以露脸，也可以实时给你看房间。拒绝视频，就可以不用再聊了。
- **核对信息是否一致**。名字、学校或工作、照片，在资料和聊天里要对得上。
- **问清楚还有谁住、谁常来**。"男朋友基本天天在"会彻底改变这个家的氛围。
- **查一下地址**。确认是真实的住宅楼，房源照片和街景对得上。

### 看房的时候

- **白天去，带个朋友**，或者把实时位置分享给信任的人。
- **见到真正的室友**，而不只是负责出租的那个人。
- **检查卧室门锁**，看看大门、走廊和楼里是否让人放心。
- **相信直觉**。逼你当场决定、或者要你晚上一个人过来的，直接离开。

### 付钱之前

- **没看房、没签书面协议，绝不付钱**，"先转定金帮你留房"是最常见的套路。
- **确认对方有权出租**：请对方出示租约，或确认你面对的是房东本人或经过认证的中介。
- **用可追踪的方式付款**，比如e-transfer，每一笔都要收据。

骗子特别喜欢用"限女生"的帖子，因为这类房源抢手，女生又容易急着抢一个"安全"的房间。更多常见骗局可以看[多伦多租房诈骗](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 住进房东家的女生要多问几句

刚落地的留学生和新移民，常常先租"房东家里的一个房间"，有时房东是一位单身男士，或者房东的成年儿子也住在家里。这种情况并不一定有问题，但因为RTA往往不适用，你的保护几乎全靠书面协议，所以要多问几句：

- 家里一共住几个人，都是谁？有没有人经常出差或长期在家？
- 房东什么情况下会进你的房间？最好写明"除紧急情况外，须经本人同意才可进入"。
- 卫生间是否和房东共用？门锁是否完好？
- 如果住得不舒服想搬走，需要提前多久通知？押金怎么退？

把这些写进协议，双方签字各留一份。真的遇到让你不安的言行，先保护自己的安全，保存证据，再寻求帮助，不要因为"刚来、不想惹麻烦"就忍着。

## 入住当天检查

- [ ] 签好室友协议，包括访客和过夜规则
- [ ] 租约或房东协议的副本存好
- [ ] 把紧急联系人告诉朋友或家人
- [ ] 拿到自己的钥匙，卧室门锁好用
- [ ] 记下楼宇问题找谁：房东、物业经理或管理员

## 找一个让你安心的室友

## 常见问题

**被室友或房东性骚扰怎么办？**
有危险请立即打911。安省人权法对住房中的性骚扰也有规定，包括来自房东、房东的代理人或同一栋楼其他住户的骚扰。保存好聊天记录，写下发生的时间和经过，再联系人权法律支援中心（Human Rights Legal Support Centre）或社区法律诊所了解你的选择。

**可以要求未来室友出示身份证件吗？**
可以，双方互相确认身份是合理的，比如视频时或看房时出示带照片的证件。只核对名字和照片就够了，不要把SIN号码、护照扫描件或银行信息发给没见过面的人。

**女生合租就是不能带男生回来吗？**
不一定。谁来租房间和谁可以来做客是两回事。访客和过夜规则要整屋人一起商量，写进室友协议，免得以后有人觉得被冒犯。

**"限女生"的房子就一定更安全吗？**
不是。"限女生"只说明租给谁，不能说明这些人怎么样。正因为这类房源抢手，骗子特别爱用，所以房东和室友一样要仔细核实，任何催你看房前先付钱的人都要远离。

**帖子写"限女生"，联系后却是男生在操作，正常吗？**
帖子和实际联系人对不上，就是一个警示信号。要求和真正的室友视频，并请对方证明有权出租这个房间。说法前后不一的话，就停止联系，并向平台举报。

## 参考资料

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（第5条）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Human Rights Legal Support Centre](https://www.hrlsc.on.ca/)

# How Much Rent Can I Afford in Toronto? (2026)

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/how-much-rent-can-i-afford-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

How much rent can I afford in Toronto? Use the 30% rule as a starting point, budget for the extras, see how roommates change the math, and know your rights.

How much rent can you afford in Toronto? A common starting point is to keep rent at or below about 30% of your before-tax income, which means multiplying your monthly rent by 40 to see the yearly salary it implies. Then check the result against your take-home pay and your other costs, because utilities, internet, insurance and transit can add a lot. If the numbers don't work for a place on your own, sharing with roommates is the most reliable way to bring rent into range.

This guide turns that rule of thumb into a real monthly budget, shows how roommates change the math, and explains what Ontario landlords can and can't do with your income information.

## Key takeaways

- **30% is a guide, not a law.** It's useful for planning, but your fixed costs, debts and savings goals matter just as much.
- **Quick math:** monthly rent × 40 = the yearly before-tax income the 30% rule suggests.
- **Budget for the extras.** Rent is only the biggest line; utilities, internet, tenant insurance and transit come on top.
- **Roommates change everything.** A room or a shared two-bedroom can cut your housing cost dramatically.
- **"3x rent" isn't the whole story in Ontario.** Landlords may consider income, but not as a rigid cut-off on its own.

## How much rent can I afford in Toronto?

Start with the simple version, then refine it.

### Step 1: The 30 percent rule for rent

Take your **before-tax annual income**, multiply by 0.30, and divide by 12. That's the monthly housing cost the rule suggests.

- $48,000 a year → about $1,200 a month
- $60,000 a year → about $1,500 a month
- $80,000 a year → about $2,000 a month

CMHC uses the same 30% line when it defines affordable housing, which is why you see it everywhere. It works best as a ceiling for planning, not a target to spend up to.

### Step 2: Check it against take-home pay

You pay rent from what actually lands in your account. After income tax, CPP and EI deductions, your take-home pay is noticeably lower than your gross salary. If rent would take close to half of your take-home pay, the rest of your month will feel tight, especially in winter when heating bills rise in some homes.

### Step 3: Add everything else

Use this worksheet. Fill in your own numbers, since costs vary by home and provider.

| Monthly cost | Notes | Your number |
|---|---|---|
| Rent (your share) | The biggest line | |
| Hydro, heat and water | Often included in room rentals; many condos bill hydro separately | |
| Internet and phone | Usually included in rooms, rarely in whole units | |
| Tenant insurance | Often required by the lease; covers your belongings and liability | |
| Transit or car | TTC has a monthly fare cap with PRESTO; a car adds insurance, gas and parking | |
| Groceries and household | Cooking at home with roommates usually saves money | |
| Debt payments and savings | Student loans, credit cards, an emergency fund | |
| Buffer | Something for surprises | |

If the total leaves no room for savings, the place is probably too expensive for you right now, even if it technically fits the 30% rule.

## Salary needed to rent in Toronto

Here's what the 30% rule implies for typical Toronto rents. These are averages, not quotes.

| Type of rental | Reference rent | Yearly income suggested by the 30% rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unfurnished one-bedroom, City of Toronto | $1,969 average asking rent | About $79,000 | liv.rent, October 2026 |
| Room in a shared home | About $1,150–$1,220 average | About $46,000–$49,000 | City of Toronto and U of T Housing Finder data, compiled by U of T Student Life, 2026 |

The gap between those two rows is the whole case for sharing. For a fuller picture of rents by home type and what's included, see our pillar guide to the [cost of renting a room in Toronto](/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/).

## How roommates change affordability

Sharing doesn't just split the rent; it splits many of the extras too.

- **A room in a shared home** is the cheapest way in, often with utilities and internet included.
- **A shared two-bedroom** gives each person a private room plus a living room, often at a per-person cost close to a single room.
- **Renting a whole house as a group, room by room** can work well for friends or matched roommates, with each person paying for their own room.

A few cautions:

- If you're **co-tenants** on one lease, each of you is generally responsible to the landlord for the **full** rent, not just your share. Choose people whose finances you trust.
- **Unequal rooms should cost different amounts.** Our guide to [how to split rent with roommates](/blog/split-rent-fairly/) walks through fair methods.
- Put the split, the bills and what happens if someone leaves in a written roommate agreement.

## Rent to income ratio in Ontario: what landlords can ask

Many landlords informally look for rent at about a third of monthly income, often phrased as "income of 3x rent." Ontario's rules are more nuanced.

### Can a landlord ask for 3x rent income?

A landlord **can ask about income**. Under Ontario's Human Rights Code and its regulation on landlord business practices (O. Reg. 290/98), landlords may ask for rental history, credit references and credit checks, and may consider income information **together with** those details. According to the Ontario Human Rights Commission:

- Income information should be used to **confirm you have enough income to pay the rent**, not as a strict cut-off.
- Applying a **rigid rent-to-income ratio**, such as a 30% cut-off, is **illegal** unless you're applying for subsidized (rent-geared-to-income) housing.
- Income can be considered on its own only when no other information, such as rental history or credit references, is available.
- **A lack of rental or credit history** should not count against you, which matters for newcomers and students.

Ontario courts have upheld a finding that refusing applicants solely on rent-to-income ratios or minimum income criteria was discriminatory.

### How to show you can pay without a "3x" income

- A letter of employment or job offer
- Proof of savings or funds, such as bank statements or a student's proof of funds
- References from previous landlords, in Canada or abroad
- Applying with roommates, so the landlord sees combined ability to pay

Our guide to [renting with no credit history in Canada](/blog/renting-with-no-credit-history-canada/) covers these documents in detail.

This is general information, not legal advice. If you believe you were refused housing because of a rigid income rule or the source of your income, contact the Human Rights Legal Support Centre or a community legal clinic.

## FAQ

**What is the 30 percent rule for rent?**
It's a rule of thumb that housing costs should take no more than about 30% of your before-tax income. CMHC uses the same 30% line to define affordable housing. It's a planning guide, not a legal limit, and many Toronto renters spend more, which is one reason sharing is so common.

**What salary do I need to rent in Toronto?**
Using the 30% rule, multiply the monthly rent by 40 to get the yearly before-tax income it suggests. For the City of Toronto average unfurnished one-bedroom asking rent of $1,969 in liv.rent's October 2026 report, that works out to roughly $79,000 a year. A shared room costs far less, so the income it implies is much lower too.

**Can a landlord refuse me because my income comes from savings or social assistance?**
Not simply for that reason. The Ontario Human Rights Commission says a landlord can't turn someone away just because their income comes from a source other than a job, such as savings, a pension or social assistance, and receiving public assistance is a protected ground in housing. Landlords can still check that you can afford the rent.

**How do I budget if my income is irregular?**
Base your rent on your lower-earning months, not your best ones, and keep a buffer of at least a month or two of rent in savings. When you apply, bank statements covering several months, contracts or invoices help show a landlord your average income.

**Should I use gross or take-home pay for my rent budget?**
The 30% rule is usually quoted on before-tax (gross) income, but you pay rent from take-home pay. Check your budget against your net pay as well: if rent takes close to half of what lands in your account, the rest of your budget will feel very tight.

## Sources

- [October 2026 Ontario rent report (liv.rent)](https://liv.rent/blog/rent-reports/october-2026-ontario-rent-report/)
- [Rental costs in Toronto/GTA (U of T Student Life, 2026)](https://www.studentlife.utoronto.ca/task/rental-costs-in-toronto-gta/)
- [Average asking rents fall 3.2% in October (CTV News, Rentals.ca and Urbanation data, Nov. 5, 2026)](https://www.ctvnews.ca/business/real-estate/article/average-asking-rents-fall-32-in-october-but-prices-rising-in-toronto-vancouver/)
- [Policy on human rights and rental housing (Ontario Human Rights Commission)](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/policy-human-rights-and-rental-housing)
- [Human rights for tenants brochure (Ontario Human Rights Commission)](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/human-rights-tenants-brochure)
- [O. Reg. 290/98: Business practices permissible to landlords (Ontario e-Laws)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980290)
- [CMHC: National Housing Strategy glossary (affordability)](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/nhs/guidepage-strategy/glossary)
- [Human Rights Legal Support Centre](https://hrlsc.on.ca/)

# 多伦多收入多少能租房？房租预算一次算清

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/how-much-rent-can-i-afford-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

多伦多收入多少能租房？用30%法则算出房租上限，把水电网、保险、交通一起列进预算，看合租怎么省钱，并讲清房东要求收入是房租3倍是否合法，新移民和留学生必看。

多伦多收入多少能租房？最常用的算法是：**房租不超过税前收入的30%左右**，反过来就是"月租乘以40"，得出建议的税前年收入。算完之后，还要拿到手工资对照一遍，再把水电、网费、租客保险和交通费都加进去，因为这些加起来不是小数目。如果一个人租整套怎么算都不够，和室友合租是把房租压下来最可靠的办法。

很多刚来多伦多的留学生和新移民，第一次找房时最关心两个问题：我这点收入能租什么样的房子？房东要求"收入是房租3倍"，是不是达不到就没戏？下面一次讲清楚。

## 先看要点

- **30%是参考，不是法律**：适合用来做规划，但你的固定开支、贷款和存钱目标同样重要。
- **快速算法**：月租 × 40 = 30%法则建议的税前年收入。
- **别忘了额外开支**：房租只是最大的一项，水电网、租客保险、交通都要另算。
- **合租能大幅降低成本**：单间或两室合租，住房开支能少一大截。
- **"3倍收入"在安省不是硬杠杠**：房东可以了解收入，但不能只用一个死板的比例来拒绝你。

## 房租占收入多少合适？

### 第一步：用30%法则算上限

用**税前年收入**乘以0.3，再除以12，就是建议的每月住房开支上限：

- 年收入4.8万加元 → 每月约1,200加元
- 年收入6万加元 → 每月约1,500加元
- 年收入8万加元 → 每月约2,000加元

加拿大按揭和住房公司 (CMHC) 定义可负担住房时，用的也是30%这条线。把它当作"上限"而不是"目标"，不要觉得没花到30%就亏了。

### 第二步：用到手工资再核对一次

房租是从到手工资里付的。扣掉个人所得税、养老金 (CPP) 和就业保险 (EI) 之后，到手的钱比税前少不少。如果房租要占到手工资的一半左右，剩下的日子会过得很紧，尤其是冬天有些房子暖气费还会上涨。

### 30%法则的局限

30%法则简单好记，但不适合所有人：收入高的人，花30%在房租上可能还绰绰有余；收入低、还要还学生贷款或寄钱回家的人，30%可能已经太多。还有，它只看房租，不看你住得远近带来的交通成本。所以最好把它和下面的完整预算表一起用。

## 多伦多一个人生活费：把每一项列出来

下面这张表帮你把每月开支列清楚。各家价格不一样，数字请按你自己的情况填。

| 每月开支 | 说明 | 你的金额 |
|---|---|---|
| 房租（你的份额） | 最大的一项 | |
| 电、暖气、水 | 合租单间常常包含；很多公寓电费单独计量 | |
| 网费和手机 | 单间一般包网，整租很少包 | |
| 租客保险 | 租约常要求购买，保障个人物品和责任 | |
| 交通 | 用 PRESTO 坐 TTC 有月度封顶；开车还有保险、油费、停车 | |
| 买菜和日用品 | 和室友一起做饭通常更省 | |
| 还款和存钱 | 学生贷款、信用卡、应急资金 | |
| 机动 | 留一点应付意外 | |

如果算完一分钱都存不下，那这套房子对你现在来说可能就太贵了，哪怕它刚好符合30%法则。

### 留学生和新移民的特别开支

刚落地的头几个月，开支往往比之后高：要买床垫、锅碗瓢盆，第一次交房租时还要同时付首月房租和最后一个月房租押金，可能还有可退的钥匙押金。按安省规定，受《住宅租赁法》保护的租赁不能收"损坏押金"。建议提前留出这笔启动资金，不要把存款全压在房租上。

## 多伦多收入多少能租房：按房型看

下面用有出处的平均租金，按30%法则换算建议年收入。这些是平均数，不是报价。

| 房型 | 参考月租 | 30%法则建议的税前年收入 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 多伦多市无家具一室一厅 | 平均挂牌价1,969加元 | 约7.9万加元 | liv.rent，2026年10月 |
| 合租房间 | 平均约1,150至1,220加元 | 约4.6万至4.9万加元 | 多伦多市和多大校外租房平台数据，多大 Student Life 汇总，2026年 |

两行之间的差距，就是合租最有说服力的理由。各类房型的租金、包含哪些费用，可以看我们的支柱文章 [多伦多租房多少钱](/zh/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/)。

## 合租怎么改变你的预算

合租不只是分房租，很多额外开支也一起分摊了：

- **合租单间**：入门最便宜，常常包水电网。
- **两人合租两室**：每人一间卧室，还有客厅，人均成本常常接近一个单间。
- **几个人整租一栋房子、按房间分别付**：适合朋友或匹配好的室友，每人为自己的房间付钱。

几点提醒：

- 如果你们是同一份租约上的**共同租客**，每个人通常都要对房东负责**全部**房租，而不只是自己那份。要选经济上靠得住的室友。
- **房间大小不一样，价格也应该不一样**，具体方法见 [合租房租怎么分](/zh/blog/split-rent-fairly/)。
- 房租怎么分、账单怎么付、有人提前搬走怎么办，最好写进书面室友协议。

## 房东要求收入是房租3倍合法吗？

不少房东会说"收入要达到房租的3倍"，也就是房租占月收入三分之一左右。但在安省，规则没那么简单。

根据安省《人权法》(Human Rights Code) 和关于房东商业行为的条例 (O. Reg. 290/98)，房东可以要求你提供租房记录、信用推荐和信用报告，并且可以**结合这些信息**考虑你的收入情况。安省人权委员会 (Ontario Human Rights Commission) 的立场是：

- 收入信息只应该用来**确认你有足够收入付房租**，而不是当作硬性门槛。
- 除了申请政府补贴的按收入定租住房 (rent-geared-to-income) 以外，房东使用**死板的房租收入比**（比如30%一刀切）是**违法**的。
- 只有在没有租房记录、信用推荐等其他信息时，才可以单独看收入。
- **没有租房记录或信用记录**不应该成为对你不利的理由，这一点对新移民和留学生很重要。

安省法院也维持过这样的认定：只凭房租收入比或最低收入标准拒绝申请人，属于歧视。

### 收入不到"3倍"，怎么证明付得起？

- 工作证明信或录用通知
- 存款证明、银行流水，留学生可以提供资金证明
- 以前房东的推荐信（国内的也可以，最好附英文翻译）
- 和室友一起申请，让房东看到合计的支付能力

更多准备材料的方法，见 [没有信用记录怎么租房](/zh/blog/renting-with-no-credit-history-canada/)。

另外提醒：在微信群、小红书或51.ca上，偶尔有人声称"不看收入、交半年房租就能租"。一次性预付大笔房租风险很高，遇到骗子钱就难追回。按安省《住宅租赁法》，房东能收的租金押金最多相当于一个月房租，交钱前一定要先看房、签好租约。

以上是一般性信息，不构成法律建议。如果你认为自己因为死板的收入标准或收入来源被拒租，可以联系人权法律支援中心 (Human Rights Legal Support Centre) 或社区法律诊所。

## 常见问题

**房租占收入多少合适？**
常用的经验法则是房租不超过税前收入的30%左右，加拿大按揭和住房公司 (CMHC) 定义"可负担住房"时也用30%这条线。它只是规划参考，不是法律规定；很多多伦多租客实际花得更多，这也是合租如此普遍的原因。

**在多伦多年薪多少才能自己租一室一厅？**
按30%法则，把月租乘以40，就是建议的税前年收入。liv.rent 2026年10月报告显示，多伦多市无家具一室一厅的平均挂牌月租为1,969加元，换算下来约需年薪7.9万加元。合租一个房间便宜得多，对收入的要求也低得多。

**收入来自存款或政府补助，房东可以因此拒绝我吗？**
不能仅凭这一点拒绝。安省人权委员会 (OHRC) 表示，房东不能只因为你的收入不是来自工作（例如存款、养老金或社会救助）就拒租，领取公共援助在住房方面属于受保护的理由。房东仍然可以核实你是否付得起房租。

**收入不固定，房租预算怎么定？**
按收入较低的月份来定房租，而不是按最好的月份；存款里最好留出一到两个月的房租作缓冲。申请时，提供几个月的银行流水、合同或发票，可以帮房东了解你的平均收入。

**留学生没有工作收入，怎么证明付得起房租？**
可以提供资金证明（银行存款证明或流水）、录取信、学签，以及以前的房东推荐信。和室友一起申请，让房东看到大家合计的支付能力，也是常见做法。

## 参考资料

- [U of T Student Life：Rental costs in Toronto/GTA（多大汇总的租金数据，2026）](https://www.studentlife.utoronto.ca/task/rental-costs-in-toronto-gta/)
- [Ontario Human Rights Commission：Policy on human rights and rental housing（安省人权委员会租房政策）](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/policy-human-rights-and-rental-housing)
- [Ontario Human Rights Commission：Human rights for tenants（租客人权手册）](https://www.ohrc.on.ca/en/human-rights-tenants-brochure)
