# Roommate Red Flags: Warning Signs Before You Move In

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/roommate-red-flags/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Roommate red flags to spot before you move in: scam warning signs, behaviour that predicts trouble, and lease set-ups that leave you exposed in Ontario.

Roommate red flags fall into three groups: scam signals (money or documents requested before you can verify anything), behaviour that predicts conflict (vagueness, disrespect, pressure), and lease set-ups that leave you without protection. One scam signal is enough to walk away; behavioural and lease red flags are reasons to slow down and ask more questions. Spotting them early is far easier than untangling a bad living situation later.

Below is a deeper checklist than the quick list in our [guide to finding a roommate in Toronto](/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/), with what each flag usually means and what to do about it.

## Key takeaways

- **Money before verification is the brightest red flag.** No deposits, "holding fees" or transfers before a viewing and a written agreement.
- **Watch how people handle questions.** Defensiveness in a 30-minute chat becomes stonewalling at month three.
- **Check the paper trail.** Who is on the lease, whether the landlord knows about you, and what you'll sign.
- **Judge behaviour, not background.** Culture, accent, religion or age tell you nothing about whether someone pays rent on time.
- **Trust the pattern.** One small flag is normal; three together is a decision.

## Roommate scam warning signs

These are deal-breakers. Scammers target busy seasons, newcomers and students who are searching from abroad.

### Money and payment red flags

1. **A deposit before you've seen the room.** A "roommate" who wants your share of first and last month's rent, or a "holding fee," before any viewing.
2. **The overpayment trick.** They send a cheque or transfer for more than they owe and ask you to send back the difference. The original payment later bounces or is reversed.
3. **Unusual payment methods.** Gift cards, cryptocurrency, wire transfers abroad or payment to a third party "handling the booking."
4. **Rent far below the area.** A private room in a prime location at a price nothing else comes close to.

### Identity and verification red flags

5. **No live video, no in-person meeting.** Constant excuses: travelling, bad connection, camera broken.
6. **Requests for your SIN, passport scans or banking logins** before you've met. A roommate never needs your SIN.
7. **A story that shifts.** The unit, the landlord's name or the reason they're overseas changes between messages.
8. **Copied photos.** The room pictures appear on other listings or hotel sites when you reverse-search them.
9. **They can't show they have the right to rent the room.** No lease, no landlord contact, no consent to sublet.

If you're unsure, our pillar on [rental scams in Toronto](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) explains how to verify a landlord or agent and what to do if you've already paid.

## Signs of a bad roommate: behaviour to watch

These aren't crimes, but they reliably predict friction. Use your first video call and in-person meeting to look for them. Our list of [questions to ask a roommate](/blog/questions-to-ask-a-roommate/) gives you the conversation starters.

### During the conversation

10. **Vague about money.** "I'll figure it out" when you ask how they'll cover rent between jobs or terms.
11. **Every past roommate was "crazy."** One bad experience is normal; a string of villains is a pattern.
12. **Dismissive of your questions.** Eye-rolling at "How do you split cleaning?" signals how real disagreements will go.
13. **Oversells being easygoing.** "I'm chill about everything" often means they haven't thought about it, or don't want to commit to anything.
14. **Pushes boundaries already.** A partner who will "only stay a few nights a week," or a pet they mention at the end.
15. **Pressure to decide today.** Legitimate roommates want a good fit too.

### What you can observe

16. **The state of their current place** on a live video call, compared with how they describe themselves.
17. **How they talk about their current landlord or roommates** in front of you.
18. **Punctuality and follow-through.** Late to every call and slow to send what they promised is a preview of bill payments.
19. **Reluctance to give a reference** from a previous landlord or roommate.

### Red flag or just different?

Not every difference is a red flag. A night-shift nurse and a 9-to-5 student can live together happily if they agree on noise. Ask whether the difference can be handled with a clear rule. If yes, it's a compatibility question. If they refuse to discuss a rule at all, that refusal is the red flag.

## Roommate red flags in the lease and set-up

These protect your money and your housing, so take them seriously even if the person seems lovely.

| Red flag | Why it matters | What to ask for |
|---|---|---|
| You won't be on the lease and they won't show the head lease | As an occupant you usually can't go to the Landlord and Tenant Board, and you can't see what the real rent is | A copy of the lease and the landlord's contact |
| "The landlord doesn't need to know" | An unapproved occupant or sublet can put the whole tenancy at risk | Written confirmation the landlord knows you'll live there |
| No written roommate agreement | Disputes become your word against theirs | A one- or two-page signed agreement |
| A "damage deposit" or non-refundable key deposit | In covered tenancies, landlords can't collect a separate damage deposit, and key deposits must be refundable | Clear receipts and what each payment is for |
| All utilities in one name with no plan | One person carries the risk and the others have no record | A written split and a shared way to track bills |
| The owner lives there and shares the kitchen, but didn't tell you | The Residential Tenancies Act generally doesn't apply in that situation | Clarity about who lives in the home |
| Pressure to sign a lease you haven't read | You may be agreeing to terms you can't keep | Time to read it, and the standard lease where required |

If your roommate is a co-tenant, remember that in Ontario each co-tenant is generally responsible to the landlord for the full rent, so vetting their finances protects you too.

This is general information, not legal advice. For questions about your rights, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.

## What to do when you spot a red flag

- **For a scam signal:** stop, don't send money or documents, and report it to the platform and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
- **For a behavioural flag:** ask a follow-up question and see how they respond. Openness is a good sign; defensiveness confirms the flag.
- **For a lease flag:** ask for the document or confirmation in writing. If they won't provide it, keep looking.
- **Already living with someone who fits the list?** Our guide to [dealing with a bad roommate](/blog/dealing-with-a-bad-roommate/) covers conversations, mediation and your options for leaving.

## Find roommates without the guesswork

## FAQ

**What are the biggest roommate red flags?**
The most serious are money requests before you have seen the room or signed anything, refusing a live video call or in-person meeting, and a story that keeps changing. After that, watch for vagueness about how they will pay rent, a history of fights with every past roommate, and resistance to putting anything in writing.

**What are the signs of a bad roommate during the first meeting?**
Pay attention to how they treat your questions. Someone who dismisses your concerns, interrupts, oversells how easygoing they are, or won't give concrete answers about cleaning, guests and money is showing you how future disagreements will go. Disrespect toward a current roommate or landlord in front of you is another warning sign.

**How do roommate scams usually work?**
Common versions include a 'roommate' who is abroad and wants a deposit before you can view, someone who sends a cheque for more than they owe and asks you to send back the difference, and people who collect deposits for a room they have no right to rent. They all depend on getting money or personal documents from you before you can verify anything.

**Should I move in if the roommate won't put me on the lease?**
Not without understanding the risks. If you're not on the lease you are usually an occupant, with few rights against the landlord and generally no access to the Landlord and Tenant Board. At minimum, see the head lease, confirm the landlord knows you will live there, and sign a written roommate agreement.

**Is it a red flag if a roommate asks for my SIN or passport?**
Yes, at the screening stage. A future roommate has no need for your Social Insurance Number, and passport or bank details should never be sent to someone you haven't met. Share only what is needed once you have seen the place and a landlord's application is genuinely in progress.

## Sources

- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)
- [Rental scam: no room for error (Competition Bureau Canada)](https://www.canada.ca/en/competition-bureau/news/2018/08/rental-scam-no-room-for-error.html)
- [Interpretation Guideline 21: Landlords, tenants, occupants (Landlord and Tenant Board)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Interpretation%20Guidelines/21%20-%20Landlords%20Tenants%20Occupants%20and%20Residential%20Tenancies.html)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies (Steps to Justice)](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)

# 室友雷区：什么样的室友不能要？

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/roommate-red-flags/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

多伦多找室友的室友雷区有哪些？从诈骗信号、相处中的危险迹象到租约安排的坑，帮你判断什么样的室友不能要，合租前先排雷，少走弯路，签约交钱前一定要看。

室友雷区大致分三类：**诈骗信号**（在你能核实之前就要钱、要证件）、**相处中的危险迹象**（含糊、不尊重、催你拍板），以及**让你毫无保障的租约安排**。碰到诈骗信号，一条就够你直接放弃；后两类则是提醒你放慢脚步、多问几句。什么样的室友不能要，越早看出来，代价越小。

在多伦多合租的留学生和新移民，大多是在微信群、小红书、51.ca 或约克论坛上找室友。这些渠道信息多、速度快，但骗子和"不靠谱的人"也混在其中。下面这份排雷清单比我们在 [多伦多找室友](/zh/blog/find-a-roommate-in-toronto/) 里列的更细，每一条都告诉你背后意味着什么、该怎么应对。

## 先看要点

- **没核实先要钱，是最大的雷**：没看房、没签协议之前，不交任何定金、"占位费"。
- **看对方怎么回答问题**：半小时聊天就防备心很重的人，住三个月后多半会冷战。
- **把书面安排查清楚**：谁在租约上、房东知不知道你、你要签什么。
- **看行为，不看背景**：口音、文化、宗教、年龄，和对方会不会按时交房租没有关系。
- **看整体**：一个小问题很正常，三个凑在一起，就该做决定了。

## 室友雷区一：诈骗信号

这一类没有商量余地。骗子最喜欢在开学季下手，专挑人还在国内、没法看房的新生。

### 钱上的雷

1. **没看房先交定金**：所谓"室友"要你先把首月和末月房租的份额、或者"占位费"转过去。
2. **超额支票套路**：对方寄来一张支票或转账，金额比应付的多，然后让你把"多的部分"转回去。过几天原来那笔钱被退回，你转出去的钱却追不回来。
3. **奇怪的付款方式**：礼品卡、加密货币、汇款到海外，或者付给一个"帮忙办手续的朋友"。
4. **价格低得离谱**：好地段的单间，价格比周边低一大截。

### 身份上的雷

5. **不肯视频、不肯见面**：总有理由，出差、信号不好、摄像头坏了。
6. **还没见面就要你的 SIN、护照扫描件或网银信息**：室友根本不需要你的社会保险号。
7. **说法前后不一致**：房子、房东名字、人在国外的原因，聊着聊着就变了。
8. **照片是盗的**：用图片搜索一查，同样的照片出现在别的房源或酒店网站上。
9. **证明不了自己有权出租**：拿不出租约，没有房东联系方式，也没有房东同意分租的证明。

拿不准的时候，可以对照我们的 [多伦多租房诈骗](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) 一文，里面讲了怎么核实房东和经纪，以及已经转了钱该怎么办。

## 室友雷区二：相处中的危险迹象

这些不犯法，但几乎一定会带来矛盾。第一次视频和见面时就可以留意。不知道问什么，可以参考 [找室友要问的问题](/zh/blog/questions-to-ask-a-roommate/)。

### 聊天时

10. **一谈钱就含糊**：问到换工作或放假期间房租怎么付，回答是"到时候再说"。
11. **每个前室友都是"奇葩"**：遇到一个不合拍的很正常，个个都是坏人，问题可能在他自己。
12. **对你的问题不耐烦**：你问"家务怎么分"，对方翻白眼，以后真有分歧也是这个态度。
13. **只会说"我很随和"**：往往是没想过这些问题，或者不想做任何承诺。
14. **一开始就试探底线**：男朋友"一周只来住几晚"，或者聊到最后才提到自己养了猫。
15. **催你今天就定**：真心想找合拍室友的人，同样希望双方都想清楚。

### 观察到的

16. **他现在住的地方什么样**：视频时看看，和他自己描述的"爱干净"对不对得上。
17. **怎么评价现任房东和室友**：当着你的面怎么说别人，以后也可能怎么说你。
18. **守不守时、说到做不做到**：每次视频都迟到、答应发的资料迟迟不发，以后交账单大概也一样。
19. **不愿意提供前房东或前室友的推荐人。**

### 是雷，还是只是不一样？

不是所有差异都是雷。上夜班的护士和朝九晚五的学生，只要约定好安静时间，也能相处得很好。判断标准是：这个差异能不能用一条明确的规则解决？能，就是磨合问题；对方连谈都不愿意谈，那才是雷。

### 华人合租圈里常见的几种情况

- **要求用人民币转到国内账户**：说是"方便你""汇率好"，但钱一出境就很难追回，也没有任何在加拿大的付款记录。
- **群里接龙"先到先得"**：用抢房的氛围逼你在看房前交钱。
- **"包水电"却限制用暖气、洗澡时间**：入住前没说清，住进去才发现各种规矩。
- **假期房间"借给朋友住"**：有人回国或放暑假时，把房间私下转给不认识的人，事先却不跟其他室友商量。

这些情况不一定都是诈骗，但都应该在入住前当面问清楚、写进协议。

## 室友雷区三：租约安排里的坑

这一类关系到你的钱和住处，哪怕对方人很好，也要认真对待。

| 雷区 | 为什么危险 | 该要求什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 你不在租约上，对方也不给你看原租约 | 作为住客 (occupant)，你通常不能去 LTB，也不知道真实房租是多少 | 原租约复印件和房东联系方式 |
| "不用告诉房东" | 房东不知情的住客或转租，可能危及整个租约 | 房东知道你入住的书面确认 |
| 没有书面室友协议 | 出了纠纷只能各说各话 | 一两页、双方签字的室友协议 |
| 收"损坏押金"或不退的钥匙押金 | 受《住宅租赁法》保护的租赁，不能另收损坏押金，钥匙押金必须可退 | 每笔钱的收据和用途说明 |
| 水电网全挂在一个人名下，也没约定 | 一个人承担全部风险，其他人没有记录 | 书面分摊方式和共同记账方法 |
| 房东自己住、共用厨房，却没提前说 | 这种情况下《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 一般不适用 | 问清楚家里到底住了谁 |
| 催你签没看过的租约 | 你可能答应了做不到的条款 | 足够的阅读时间，需要时使用标准租约 |

另外提醒：如果你和室友都是共同租客 (co-tenants)，在安省每个共同租客通常都要对房东负责**全部**房租。所以了解室友的经济状况，其实也是在保护你自己。

以上是一般性信息，不构成法律建议。关于自己的权益，可以咨询房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 或社区法律诊所。

## 发现雷区之后怎么办？

- **诈骗信号**：立刻停下，不转钱、不发证件，向发布平台和加拿大反诈骗中心 (Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre) 举报。在微信群里看到可疑帖子，也可以提醒群主。
- **相处中的迹象**：追问一句，看对方怎么反应。坦然解释是好事；马上防备，基本就坐实了。
- **租约安排的坑**：要求对方提供书面文件或确认。拿不出来，就继续找下一个。

## 常见问题

**什么样的室友不能要？**
最不能要的是没看房、没签协议就让你转钱的人，不肯视频或见面的人，以及说法前后不一致的人。其次要警惕：问到房租怎么付就含糊其辞、说起每个前室友都是"奇葩"、一提书面协议就推脱的人。

**找室友时常见的诈骗套路有哪些？**
常见的有：自称人在国外、要你先交定金才能看房；寄来一张超额支票或转账，再让你把"多出来的钱"转回去；以及根本无权出租的人收好几个人的定金。共同点都是在你能核实之前，先拿到你的钱或证件。

**不在租约上的合租有什么风险？**
如果你不在租约上，一般被视为住客 (occupant)，对房东基本没有权利，通常也不能向房东与租客委员会 (LTB) 申请。至少要看到原租约，确认房东知道你会入住，并和签约人签一份书面室友协议。

**未来室友要我的SIN或护照，正常吗？**
在初步筛选阶段不正常。室友根本不需要你的社会保险号 (SIN)，护照和银行信息也不应该发给还没见过面的人。只有看过房、确实在走房东的正式申请流程时，才提供必要的材料。

**第一次见面怎么看出室友靠不靠谱？**
重点看对方怎么对待你的问题。打断你、敷衍你、只会说"我很随和"却给不出具体答案的人，以后有分歧时多半也是这个态度。当着你的面吐槽现任房东或室友，也是一个信号。

## 参考资料

- [Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre（加拿大反诈骗中心）](https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/)
- [Rental scam: no room for error（加拿大竞争局）](https://www.canada.ca/en/competition-bureau/news/2018/08/rental-scam-no-room-for-error.html)
- [LTB Interpretation Guideline 21：房东、租客与住客](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Interpretation%20Guidelines/21%20-%20Landlords%20Tenants%20Occupants%20and%20Residential%20Tenancies.html)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease（安省标准租约指南）](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies（Steps to Justice）](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)

# 4 Month Sublet Toronto: A Student Guide to Term Housing

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/short-term-sublet-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Need a 4 month sublet in Toronto? A student guide to summer and co-op term sublets: when to look, subletting your own room, landlord consent and paperwork.

A 4 month sublet in Toronto is how many students cover a summer, a co-op work term or a semester away: someone moves into a tenant's room for one term while the original tenant stays on the lease. The two rules that matter most are simple: the tenant needs the **landlord's written consent**, which can't be arbitrarily or unreasonably refused, and everyone should sign a **written sublet agreement** that spells out dates, rent and the deposit.

This guide is for students on both sides: finding a term sublet, and subletting your own room while you're away. For the legal background on subletting in general, see our pillar guide to [sublet rules in Ontario](/blog/sublet-and-assignment-ontario/).

## Key takeaways

- **Sublet = temporary.** The original tenant plans to return and stays responsible to the landlord.
- **Consent first.** Ask the landlord in writing before anyone moves in.
- **Put it on paper:** dates, rent, deposit, utilities, furniture, keys and house rules.
- **No profit.** A tenant can't charge a subtenant more than the lawful rent.
- **Start early.** Term sublets line up with school calendars, so plan around the term you need.
- **Under 28 nights is a different category.** Very short stays fall under Toronto's [short-term rental rules](/blog/short-term-rentals-toronto/).

*This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic; many universities also have student legal services.*

## 4 month sublet Toronto: your options at a glance

| Option | Best for | What you sign | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sublet of a tenant's room | One summer or co-op term | Sublet agreement with the tenant | Tenant must have landlord consent |
| Room in a live-in owner's home | Furnished, flexible stays | Room agreement with the owner | The RTA usually doesn't apply (shared kitchen or bathroom) |
| Short fixed-term lease | You want your own lease | Lease with the landlord | Tenancy continues unless you give notice |
| Stays under 28 nights | A few weeks only | Booking or short agreement | City short-term rental rules apply |

## Timing around school terms

Most Ontario universities and colleges run three terms: **September to December**, **January to April** and **May to August**. That rhythm drives the sublet market:

- **Summer (May to August)** is the busiest time, as students head home, travel or start internships.
- **Fall and winter** sublets come from exchange students, co-op placements and graduating students.
- Students often post their rooms a month or two before a term ends, so start watching early and be ready to move quickly when a good match appears.

Line up your dates with your exams, work start date and flights. A sublet that starts on the 1st but a job that starts on the 15th can still be the right choice; just budget for it.

## Finding a summer sublet for students

### Where to look

Your school's off-campus housing listings, student groups and faculty boards, Facebook groups and roommate apps are the usual starting points. Wherever you look, sublets attract scammers because students are often searching from another city or country.

### Questions to ask the tenant

- Are you on the lease, and has your landlord agreed to this sublet in writing?
- What's included: furniture, utilities, internet, laundry?
- Who are the roommates, and what are the house rules?
- How is the deposit handled, and when exactly will it come back?
- What happens if you need to come back early, or I need to leave early?

### Red flags

- They won't show the room on a live video call or in person.
- They want a deposit before you've seen the place or signed anything.
- They can't show a lease, or the story about the landlord keeps changing.

Our guide to [rental scams in Toronto](/blog/toronto-rental-scams/) covers the most common sublet scripts.

## How to sublet your room for a term

### Step 1: Ask your landlord in writing

Send a short email: your dates, the person's name and contact, and a request for consent. Keep the reply. If the landlord refuses without a good reason, the pillar guide explains your options.

### Step 2: Talk to your roommates

They'll live with this person for four months. Let them meet the candidate, and agree on how the decision is made.

### Step 3: Screen like a landlord would

Ask for ID, school or job details and a reference. A video call plus one in-person meeting goes a long way.

### Step 4: Sign a sublet agreement

- [ ] Start and end dates, and that the room must be vacated on the end date
- [ ] Monthly rent (not more than your lawful rent), due date and how it's paid
- [ ] Deposit amount, what it covers and when it's returned
- [ ] Utilities and internet: included, or split how
- [ ] Furniture and items left behind, with photos
- [ ] Keys and fobs, and when they're returned
- [ ] House rules: guests, quiet hours, cleaning
- [ ] What happens if either side needs to end early

### Step 5: Hand over, and stay reachable

Take dated photos of the room, give the subtenant your landlord's contact for urgent repairs, and keep an eye on rent payments. You're still the tenant, so a missed payment is your problem too.

## The last week of the term

For subtenants, moving out cleanly is how you get your deposit back. Agree on a walk-through time a few days before the end date, clean to the standard you found, return every key and fob, and take dated photos as you leave. For tenants coming back, check the room against your move-in photos and return the deposit on the date in your agreement, with a short written note of any deductions. Settling up on time keeps the next sublet easy to arrange.

## Co-op term housing

Co-op and internship students coming to Toronto for one term usually want furnished, short and close to the office. A sublet often fits best. If you're offered a short fixed-term lease instead, know that in Ontario a fixed-term tenancy doesn't end on its own; to leave on the last day, you'd normally give an N9 at least 60 days before. Signing an N9 at the same time as the lease, as a condition of getting it, is generally void.

If you rent a room in an owner's home and share their kitchen or bathroom, the Residential Tenancies Act usually doesn't apply. That can be fine for one term, but get the dates, the deposit and the notice period in writing.

International students arriving for a term can find more on documents and first steps in our [international student housing guide](/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/).

## Find your term home

## FAQ

**Can my landlord say no to me subletting my room for the summer?**
You need your landlord's consent to sublet, but under section 97 of the Residential Tenancies Act they can't arbitrarily or unreasonably refuse it. A specific concern about the person you propose can be reasonable; a blanket 'never' usually isn't. If you share a kitchen or bathroom with a live-in owner, the RTA generally doesn't apply, so your agreement with the owner decides.

**Am I still responsible for rent while someone sublets my room?**
Yes. In a sublet you stay the tenant, so if your subtenant doesn't pay or damages the place, the landlord can look to you. Collect rent on a schedule that gives you time to cover a gap, and keep a written record of every payment.

**Can I charge more for my sublet than I pay?**
No. The RTA doesn't allow a tenant to charge a subtenant more than the lawful rent. Charging your share for your room, plus any utilities you've agreed to split, keeps you on the right side of the rules.

**Is a sublet of a few weeks treated differently in Toronto?**
Yes. Rentals of less than 28 consecutive nights fall under the City of Toronto's short-term rental rules, which come with registration and principal-residence requirements. A full four-month term is well beyond that threshold.

**What if my subtenant won't leave at the end of the term?**
A subtenant has no right to stay past the agreed end date. The Residential Tenancies Act gives the tenant and the landlord a way to apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board about an overholding subtenant, and there are time limits, so act quickly and get advice from a legal clinic.

## Sources

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (sections 5 and 97)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [LTB Brochure: How a Tenant Can End Their Tenancy](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/How%20a%20Tenant%20Can%20End%20Their%20Tenancy%20(EN).html)
- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [City of Toronto: Short-term rental operators and hosts](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/housing-shelter/rental-housing-rights-information/short-term-rentals/short-term-rental-operators-hosts/)
- [CLEO: Moving out, subletting and assigning](https://www.cleo.on.ca/en/publications/subassign/all)

# 多伦多短租：留学生4个月短租与暑假转租指南

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/short-term-sublet-toronto/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

多伦多短租怎么找？留学生4个月短租、暑假转租和co-op实习住房全攻略：什么时候找、怎样把自己的房间转租出去、房东同意和协议怎么写、如何防骗。

多伦多短租，对留学生来说最常见的就是"4个月短租"：暑假回国、去外地实习、交换一个学期时，把自己的房间转租（sublet）给别人住一个学期，自己仍然留在租约上。最关键的两条规则很简单：转租需要**房东书面同意**，而房东不能任意或不合理地拒绝；双方要签一份**书面转租协议**，写清日期、房租和押金。

每到三四月，微信群、小红书、51.ca、约克论坛上就会冒出大量"暑假转租""求4个月短租"的帖子。这篇站在两边讲：想找短租的同学，和想把房间转出去、又不想白白多付几个月房租的同学。转租的完整法律规则，可以看我们的[安省转租规定](/zh/blog/sublet-and-assignment-ontario/)。

## 要点速览

- **转租是临时的**：原租客打算回来，并且继续对房东负责。
- **先拿同意**：有人搬进来之前，书面问房东。
- **白纸黑字**：日期、房租、押金、水电网、家具、钥匙、家规都写进协议。
- **不能赚差价**：租客不能向转租人收取超过合法租金的费用。
- **早点开始**：短租跟着学期走，按你需要的学期提前规划。
- **少于28晚是另一回事**：只住几个星期的，属于多伦多市政府的短期出租规则。

*本文为一般信息，不构成法律意见。具体情况请咨询房东租客委员会（LTB）或社区法律诊所，很多大学也有学生法律服务（student legal services）。*

## 多伦多短租有哪几种？

| 类型 | 适合 | 签什么 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 转租某个租客的房间 | 一个暑假或一个实习学期 | 和租客签转租协议 | 租客必须有房东同意 |
| 住进房东家的单间 | 带家具、时间灵活 | 和房东签房间协议 | 共用厨卫时RTA一般不适用 |
| 自己签一份短期定期租约 | 想要自己的租约 | 和房东签租约 | 到期不会自动结束，要提前通知 |
| 少于28晚的短住 | 只住几个星期 | 预订或简单协议 | 适用市政府短期出租规则 |

关于最后一种：多伦多规定，连续少于28晚的出租属于短期出租（short-term rental），出租人必须向市政府登记，而且只能出租自己的主要住所（principal residence）。一个完整的4个月学期远远超过28晚，不在这个范围内。

## 4个月短租：跟着学期走

安省大多数大学和学院一年三个学期：**9月到12月**、**1月到4月**、**5月到8月**。短租市场也跟着这个节奏走：

- **暑假（5月到8月）**最热闹，大家回国、旅行或者开始实习；
- **秋季和冬季**的转租多来自交换生、co-op实习生和毕业生；
- 很多同学会在学期结束前一两个月就发帖，所以要早点盯着，看到合适的就尽快决定。

日期要和考试、入职时间、机票一起对。房子1号起租但工作15号才开始，也可能值得，只要把多出来的半个月算进预算就行。

## 暑假转租：找房的同学看这里

### 去哪里找

学校的校外住房平台、学生会和院系群、Facebook群、室友App，以及华人常用的微信群、小红书、51.ca、约克论坛。渠道越多越好，但要记住：转租帖是骗子的重灾区，因为很多同学人还在国内或外地，没法当面看房。

### 要问原租客的问题

- 你在租约上吗？房东书面同意这次转租了吗？
- 包括哪些：家具、水电、网络、洗衣？
- 室友是谁？有什么家规？
- 押金怎么处理？哪一天退？
- 如果你要提前回来，或者我要提前走，怎么办？

### 危险信号

- 不肯视频实时看房，也不肯当面看；
- 没看房、没签字就要定金；
- 拿不出租约，关于房东的说法前后不一。

更多常见套路见[多伦多租房诈骗](/zh/blog/toronto-rental-scams/)。

## 把自己的房间转租出去：五步走

**第一步：书面问房东。**发一封简短邮件，写明日期、接手人的名字和联系方式，请求同意，回复要保存好。

**第二步：和室友商量。**他们要和这个人一起住四个月，让他们见一见，商量好怎么拍板。

**第三步：像房东一样筛选。**看证件、学校或工作信息，要一个推荐人。一次视频加一次见面，能排除大部分问题。

**第四步：签转租协议。**

- [ ] 起止日期，并写明到期必须搬出
- [ ] 月租（不超过你的合法租金）、交租日和付款方式
- [ ] 押金金额、用途和退还时间
- [ ] 水电网是包含还是怎么分摊
- [ ] 留下的家具和物品，附照片
- [ ] 钥匙和门禁卡，以及归还时间
- [ ] 家规：访客、安静时间、打扫
- [ ] 任何一方需要提前结束时怎么办

**第五步：交接，并保持联系。**拍下带日期的房间照片，把房东的维修联系方式给接手人，留意每月房租是否按时到账。你仍然是租客，少交一笔就是你的问题。

### 回国或出发前的准备

把房间交给别人住四个月，出发前多做几件小事，回来时会省心很多：

- **贵重物品带走或锁好**：证件、电子产品、首饰不要留在房间里；留下的家具和电器拍照登记。
- **问一下你的租客保险**：确认有人转租期间，你留下的物品是否还在保障范围内，不确定就打电话问保险公司。
- **水电网账户**：如果账户在你名下，约定好接手人怎么把他那份转给你，账单截图发给对方。
- **信件和包裹**：请室友帮忙收，或者提前改好重要账户的地址。
- **留下联系方式**：给接手人和室友一个你在国内也能用的联系方式，比如微信加邮箱，有维修或紧急情况能及时找到你。
- **告诉房东接手人的名字和日期**：就算已经拿到同意，出发前再确认一次，免得房东看到陌生人以为出了问题。

### 学期最后一周

对接手的同学来说，干净地搬走才能顺利拿回押金：结束前几天约好验房时间，打扫到入住时的样子，归还所有钥匙和门禁卡，离开时拍照留底。对回来的原租客来说，对照入住照片检查房间，按协议日期退押金，有扣款就书面写明原因。准时结清，下次再转租也容易。

## Co-op实习住房

来多伦多实习一个学期的co-op学生，最想要的通常是带家具、短期、离公司近。转租往往最合适。如果对方给你的是一份短期定期租约，要知道在安省，定期租约到期不会自动结束；想在最后一天搬走，一般要至少提前60天交N9。签租约时被要求同时签N9、并以此作为租房条件，一般是无效的。

如果你住进房东家、和房东共用厨房或卫生间，住宅租赁法（Residential Tenancies Act, RTA）通常不适用。住一个学期没问题，但日期、押金和通知期一定要写下来。刚到加拿大的同学，可以再看看[多伦多留学生租房指南](/zh/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/)，了解需要准备的材料。

## 找到这个学期的家

## 常见问题

**暑假想把房间转租出去，房东可以不同意吗？**
转租需要房东同意，但根据RTA第97条，房东不能任意或不合理地拒绝。针对具体人选的真实顾虑可能算合理，一概说"不行"通常不算。如果你和同住房东共用厨房或卫生间，RTA一般不适用，就看你和房东的协议。

**房间转租出去后，房租出了问题谁负责？**
你。转租期间你仍然是租客，接手的人不交房租或弄坏东西，房东可以找你。所以收租时间要留出余地，每一笔都留记录。

**转租可以比我自己付的房租收得高吗？**
不可以。RTA不允许租客向转租人收取超过合法租金的费用。按你房间的份额收，再加上事先约定好分摊的水电网，就不会有问题。

**短租只住几个星期，规则一样吗？**
不一样。在多伦多，连续少于28晚的出租属于市政府的短期出租（short-term rental）规则管辖，涉及登记和主要住所等要求。完整的4个月学期远远超过这个门槛。

**转租到期了对方不搬走怎么办？**
转租人没有权利在约定结束日之后继续住。住宅租赁法为租客和房东提供了就超期不走的转租人向LTB申请的途径，而且有时间限制，所以要尽快行动，并向法律诊所咨询。

## 参考资料

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006（第5、97条）](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [LTB Brochure: How a Tenant Can End Their Tenancy](https://tribunalsontario.ca/documents/ltb/Brochures/How%20a%20Tenant%20Can%20End%20Their%20Tenancy%20(EN).html)
- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [City of Toronto: Short-term rental operators and hosts](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/housing-shelter/rental-housing-rights-information/short-term-rentals/short-term-rental-operators-hosts/)
- [CLEO: Moving out, subletting and assigning](https://www.cleo.on.ca/en/publications/subassign/all)

# International Student Cap and Toronto Rent: 2026 Update

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/student-cap-toronto-rent/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

How the international student cap affected Toronto rent as of November 2026: softer prices near many campuses, why rent near U of T held up, and student tips.

The international student cap has eased Toronto rent pressure, but less than in many other cities: as of November 2026, fewer new study permits helped cool rents near many Ontario campuses, while rent near the University of Toronto held up because downtown demand comes from far more than students. In practice, students now have more choice and more room to negotiate than in 2022 or 2023, especially near suburban colleges. Toronto as a whole, though, saw asking rents tick up again in October 2026.

## Key takeaways

- **Fewer permits:** IRCC expects to issue up to 408,000 study permits in 2026, including about 155,000 for new arrivals, roughly 7% below 2025's target.
- **Campus-area rents softened in many cities,** according to Rentals.ca's October 2025 analysis, with the steepest declines in Ontario and B.C. markets that relied heavily on international enrolment.
- **Toronto was the exception:** rents near U of T rose 7.3% in that analysis, even as citywide rents fell 6.4%.
- **The cap isn't the only cause.** CMHC also points to record new rental supply, slower population growth and a softer job market.
- **Toronto's average asking rent rose 1.6% year over year in October 2026** (Rentals.ca and Urbanation), so don't count on prices falling further.

## How the international student cap changed Toronto rent

Canada introduced a cap on new study permit applications in 2024 and tightened it again for 2025 and 2026. IRCC's 2026 plan expects up to 408,000 permits issued in total: about 155,000 for newly arriving students and 253,000 extensions for current and returning students. That compares with targets of 437,000 for 2025 and 485,000 for 2024.

Fewer students arriving means fewer people hunting for rooms each August, and the effect shows up in the data:

- **Population:** Statistics Canada estimated that Canada's population fell slightly in the first quarter of 2026, the third quarterly decline in a row, driven by a shrinking number of non-permanent residents.
- **Vacancy:** CMHC's 2025 Rental Market Report found Toronto's purpose-built vacancy rate reached 3%, the first time at that level since the pandemic, and listed weaker international student demand among the reasons.
- **Campus areas:** Rentals.ca reported that renter inquiries (leads) for listings near campuses fell 39%, compared with a 28% drop nationally, in its October 2025 study.

### Why causation is tricky

The cap arrived at the same moment as a record wave of new condo and purpose-built rental completions, a softer job market and wider immigration cuts. All of these push rents the same way. So it's fair to say the cap contributed to cooler student rental markets, but not that it single-handedly lowered Toronto rents.

## Rent near U of T: why it held up

Rentals.ca's 2025 analysis looked at listings within 1.5 km of main campuses. Near the University of Toronto's downtown campus, average rents rose 7.3%, while Toronto overall fell 6.4%. Rentals.ca put it down to demand from non-student renters in the downtown core, a market where students are only one group among many.

That pattern makes sense. The Annex, Kensington Market and the streets around Spadina and College aren't student enclaves; they're some of Toronto's most sought-after neighbourhoods. When students leave, other renters quickly fill the gap.

What this means if you're heading to U of T St. George:

- Expect competition for well-priced rooms, especially from May to September.
- Consider a short subway or streetcar ride. Areas along Line 1 north of Bloor or Line 2 east and west can offer better value with a direct commute.
- Share a larger unit. Splitting a two- or three-bedroom often costs about the same per person as a single room but comes with more space.

Our guide to the [best neighbourhoods in Toronto for students](/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/) compares areas near each major campus.

## Is it easier to find student housing now?

For most students, yes, somewhat: there are more listings and fewer people competing for them than at the 2022 to 2023 peak. But it depends a lot on where you're looking.

| Area | What the data suggest (as of late 2026) | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Downtown, near U of T St. George | Rents held up in Rentals.ca's 2025 campus study; non-student demand keeps prices firm | Start early; look a few stops out |
| Neighbourhoods near Toronto-area colleges | Rentals.ca data reported by the Globe and Mail showed rents near Ontario colleges falling faster than citywide | Ask about incentives; check the home is legal |
| Ontario cities that relied heavily on international students, such as London | Some of the clearest softening; CMHC reported London's vacancy at 4% in 2025 | Useful context if you're still choosing a school |
| Toronto overall | Asking rents up 1.6% year over year in October 2026 | Don't wait for a further drop |

More choice also means you can be pickier. Don't settle for an overcrowded house, a basement without proper exits or a landlord who wants cash before you've seen the room. With more vacancies, legitimate landlords have every reason to treat good tenants well.

### Already renting? Use the extra choice

If you're mid-lease, the market doesn't change your rent until renewal, and for most older units any increase is capped by Ontario's guideline (2.1% for 2026). But a softer market can still work for you. If your current place is overcrowded, far from campus or unsafe, compare what similar money buys today; you may be able to move somewhere better at a similar cost. Just give proper written notice before you leave, usually 60 days before the end of a lease or rental period, so you're not paying for two places at once.

### A quick checklist before you sign

- Verify the landlord's identity and that they own or manage the unit.
- Never send a deposit for a room you haven't seen, in person or on a live video call.
- Get the Ontario Standard Lease where it applies, and read it before you pay.
- Ask who else lives there, and whether you'd share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner.
- Budget for first month's rent plus a last month's deposit; damage deposits aren't allowed in Ontario.

Our pillar guide to [international student housing in Toronto](/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/) walks through leases, deposits and your rights step by step, and the [cost of renting a room in Toronto](/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/) guide helps you set a realistic budget.

## What to watch next

Toronto's overall asking rents rose 1.6% year over year in October 2026, the first annual increase in nearly three years, according to Rentals.ca and Urbanation, as fewer new buildings come to market. If new construction keeps slowing while student numbers stabilize, the extra choice students enjoy today may narrow. IRCC's next levels plan and its 2027 cap allocations will be worth watching.

## Find your people, not just a room

## FAQ

**How many study permits will Canada issue in 2026?**
IRCC said in November 2025 that it expects to issue up to 408,000 study permits in 2026: about 155,000 for newly arriving students and 253,000 extensions for students already here. That's about 7% below the 2025 target of 437,000.

**Did the student cap cause Toronto rents to fall?**
It was one factor among several. CMHC and rent analysts list fewer international students alongside record new rental supply, slower population growth and a weaker job market. It's hard to separate the effects, so be wary of anyone who credits the cap alone.

**Do master's and PhD students need a provincial attestation letter in 2026?**
IRCC said that as of January 1, 2026, master's and doctoral students at public designated learning institutions don't need a provincial or territorial attestation letter. They still count toward the overall number of permits issued. Always confirm current rules on canada.ca.

**Is on-campus residence cheaper than renting off campus in Toronto?**
Not always. Residence often bundles a meal plan and furniture, which can cost more than a shared room off campus but saves on setup costs and commuting. Compare the full monthly cost, including food, transit and utilities, before deciding.

**When should international students start looking for housing in Toronto?**
For a September start, begin seriously in June or July and avoid paying anything before you've verified the landlord. For January intake, November and December are quieter months with more room to negotiate.

## Sources

- [IRCC: 2026 provincial and territorial allocations under the international student cap](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/2026-provincial-territorial-allocations-under-international-student-cap.html)
- [Rentals.ca: Rental prices near Canadian post-secondary schools drop as international student numbers fall (October 2025)](https://press.rentals.ca/432008-rental-prices-near-canadian-post-secondary-schools-drop-as-international-student-numbers-fall)
- [Rentals.ca: Lower prices, more choice in student rentals as international student caps take effect](https://rentals.ca/blog/lower-prices-more-choice-in-student-rentals-as-international-student-caps-take-effect)
- [CMHC: Canada's vacancy rate rises amid historically high rental construction (2025 Rental Market Report)](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/media-newsroom/news-releases/2025/canadas-vacancy-rate-rises-amid-historically-high-rental-construction)
- [The Globe and Mail chart (Rentals.ca data): Rents dropping faster in Ontario neighbourhoods near colleges](https://charts.theglobeandmail.com/2oCkz/4/)

- [Rentals.ca and Urbanation: November 2026 National Rent Report (October data)](https://press.rentals.ca/476871-toronto-and-vancouver-rents-post-first-annual-increases-in-more-than-two-and-a-half-years-as-national-decline-narrows)

# 留学生配额与多伦多房租：学签收紧后好租了吗

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/student-cap-toronto-rent/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

留学生配额对多伦多房租影响多大？截至2026年11月，很多校区周边租金回落，但多大附近依然坚挺。学签收紧后好不好租、去哪找、怎么谈价，一文看懂。

留学生配额确实给多伦多房租降了温，但降得没有很多城市那么明显。截至2026年11月，新学签减少让安省不少校区周边的租金回落，可多伦多大学（多大）市中心校区附近的房租依然坚挺，因为那里的租房需求远不只来自学生。总体来说，现在留学生找房的选择比2022、2023年多，谈价空间也更大，尤其是在郊区学院附近；但多伦多整体挂牌租金在2026年10月又出现了同比小幅上涨。

## 先看重点

- **学签变少**：IRCC 预计2026年最多签发40.8万份学习许可，其中新入境学生约15.5万份，比2025年目标低约7%。
- **很多城市的校区周边租金回落**：据 Rentals.ca 2025年10月的分析，在国际学生占比高的安省和卑诗省城市，校区附近跌得最多。
- **多伦多是例外**：同一分析中，多大附近租金上涨7.3%，而全市平均下降6.4%。
- **配额不是唯一原因**：CMHC 同时提到新出租房源创纪录、人口增长放缓和就业市场疲软。
- **多伦多整体房租已经回稳**：Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 数据显示，2026年10月多伦多平均挂牌租金同比上涨1.6%，别指望还会大跌。

## 留学生配额对多伦多房租有多大影响？

加拿大从2024年开始对新的学签申请设上限，2025年和2026年又进一步收紧。按 IRCC 的2026年计划，全年预计最多签发40.8万份学习许可，包括约15.5万份新入境学生和25.3万份在读、返校学生的续签；作为对比，2025年目标为43.7万份，2024年为48.5万份。

每年8月来找房的新生少了，数据上也能看到变化：

- **人口**：加拿大统计局估计，2026年第一季度全国人口略有下降，是连续第三个季度下降，主要原因是非永久居民（包括留学生）人数减少。
- **空置率**：CMHC 2025年租赁市场报告显示，多伦多专门出租楼空置率升至3%，是疫情以来首次达到这个水平，报告把国际学生需求减弱列为原因之一。
- **校区周边**：Rentals.ca 2025年10月的研究发现，校区附近房源收到的租客询价减少了39%，而全国平均减少28%。

### 为什么不能简单说"都是配额造成的"

配额出台的同时，多伦多正好迎来大批新公寓和专门出租楼集中完工，加上就业市场转弱、整体移民收紧，这些因素都在往同一个方向推房租。所以比较准确的说法是：配额让学生租房市场降了温，但并不是多伦多房租下降的唯一原因。

## 多大附近租房：为什么没怎么降？

Rentals.ca 2025年的分析统计了各大主校区1.5公里范围内的房源。多大市中心 (St. George) 校区附近平均租金上涨7.3%，而多伦多全市下降6.4%。Rentals.ca 的解释是，市中心有大量非学生租客的需求，学生只是其中一部分。

这也很好理解。Annex、Kensington Market、Spadina 和 College 一带并不是单纯的"学生区"，而是多伦多最受欢迎的社区之一。学生少了，上班族等其他租客很快就会补上。

如果你要去多大 St. George 校区：

- 好价格的房间依然抢手，尤其是5月到9月；
- 可以考虑坐几站地铁或电车，沿1号线 Bloor 以北、2号线东西两侧往往性价比更高，通勤也直达；
- 和同学合租两室或三室，人均价格常常和单租一个房间差不多，空间却大得多。

各大校区附近有哪些社区适合住，可以看 [多伦多留学生住哪里](/zh/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-students/)。

## 学签收紧后租房好租了吗？

对大多数留学生来说，答案是：比以前好租一些。房源更多，竞争的人更少，但具体还要看你在哪里找。前几年那种"一房难求、看房要排队、当场就得交定金"的情况，在很多区域已经少见了；不过市中心热门地段依然要拼手速。

| 区域 | 数据显示的情况（截至2026年底） | 建议 |
|---|---|---|
| 市中心多大 St. George 校区附近 | Rentals.ca 2025年研究中租金不降反升，非学生需求撑住价格 | 提早找，或往外住几站 |
| 大多伦多各学院周边社区 | 据《环球邮报》引用的 Rentals.ca 数据，安省学院附近租金比全市跌得更快 | 主动问优惠，确认房子合法 |
| 伦敦 (London) 等高度依赖留学生的安省城市 | 降温最明显之一，CMHC 显示伦敦2025年空置率为4% | 还在选学校的话可作参考 |
| 多伦多整体 | 2026年10月挂牌租金同比上涨1.6% | 不要等着继续降价 |

选择多了，你也可以更挑剔一点：人数超标的合租屋、没有合格出口的地下室、没看房就要你先转账的"房东"，统统可以说不。市场空置变多，正规房东更愿意好好对待靠谱的租客。

### 在学院附近找房要注意什么

亨伯 (Humber)、圣力嘉 (Seneca)、百年理工 (Centennial)、谢尔丹 (Sheridan) 等学院的校区多在郊区，周边以独立屋和地下室出租为主。房源变多是好事，但也要留意：

- **问清楚是不是合法单位**：地下室有没有合格的出口和窗户，独立屋里一共住几个人；
- **算好通勤**：郊区公交班次少，冬天等车很辛苦，签约前查一下到校区的实际时间；
- **谈价时有底气**：可以拿同一区域的几个房源做对比，问房东能不能包网、包水电或减免第一个月；
- **一起找更划算**：和同校同学组队整租一套房，往往比各自租单间更便宜，也更安全。

### 已经在租房的同学：也可以利用这个机会

如果你租约还没到期，市场变化不会影响你现在的房租；续租时，大多数老单位的涨幅受安省指导线限制（2026年为2.1%）。但如果现在住的地方太挤、离学校太远或者不安全，可以比较一下同样的预算现在能租到什么，也许能换到更好的房子。只是记得按规定提前书面通知房东退租，一般是在租期结束前60天，免得两边同时交房租。

### 签约前自查清单

- 核实房东身份，确认对方确实是业主或物业管理方；
- 没有实地看房或视频直播看房之前，绝不转定金；
- 适用的情况下要求使用安省标准租约，付款前先读完；
- 问清楚还有谁住在这里，是否要和房东共用厨房或卫生间；
- 预留第一个月房租和最后一个月押金，安省不允许收损坏押金。

从租约、押金到租客权利，完整流程可以看 [多伦多留学生租房](/zh/blog/international-student-renting-toronto/)；预算怎么定，可以参考 [多伦多租房多少钱](/zh/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/)。

## 接下来要关注什么？

根据 Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation，2026年10月多伦多整体挂牌租金同比上涨1.6%，是近三年来首次同比上涨，原因之一是新完工的楼盘在减少。如果新建房源继续放缓，而留学生人数趋于稳定，现在学生享受的"选择多、好谈价"可能会慢慢收窄。IRCC 下一份移民配额计划和2027年学签分配，都值得留意。

## 找房，更要找对室友

## 常见问题

**2026年加拿大发多少学签？**
加拿大移民部 (IRCC) 在2025年11月表示，预计2026年最多签发40.8万份学习许可，其中约15.5万份给新入境学生，25.3万份为在读学生续签。这比2025年43.7万份的目标低约7%。

**多伦多房租下降是不是因为留学生少了？**
留学生减少是原因之一，但不是全部。CMHC 和租金分析机构同时提到大量新出租房源完工、人口增长放缓和就业市场疲软。这些因素很难完全分开，所以不要轻信"全是配额造成的"这种说法。

**2026年读硕士、博士还需要省级证明信吗？**
IRCC 表示，从2026年1月1日起，在公立指定学校 (DLI) 就读硕士和博士的学生，申请学签时不再需要省级证明信 (PAL/TAL)，但仍计入总签发数量。具体以加拿大政府官网最新说明为准。

**住学校宿舍比校外合租便宜吗？**
不一定。宿舍常常捆绑餐卡和家具，月费可能比校外合租单间高，但省去了买家具和通勤的成本。比较时要把伙食、交通、水电网都算进去。

**留学生什么时候开始在多伦多找房最好？**
9月入学的话，6、7月开始认真找，没核实房东身份之前不要付任何钱。1月入学的话，11、12月是淡季，房源竞争小，谈价空间也更大。

## 参考资料

- [IRCC：2026年国际学生配额省级分配通知](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/2026-provincial-territorial-allocations-under-international-student-cap.html)
- [Rentals.ca：国际学生减少，加拿大高校周边租金下降（2025年10月）](https://press.rentals.ca/432008-rental-prices-near-canadian-post-secondary-schools-drop-as-international-student-numbers-fall)
- [Rentals.ca：学签配额生效后，学生租房价格更低、选择更多](https://rentals.ca/blog/lower-prices-more-choice-in-student-rentals-as-international-student-caps-take-effect)
- [CMHC：2025年租赁市场报告新闻稿](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/media-newsroom/news-releases/2025/canadas-vacancy-rate-rises-amid-historically-high-rental-construction)
- [加拿大统计局：2026年第一季度人口估算](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260617/dq260617a-eng.htm)

# Toronto Rent Prices 2026: Is Rent Still Going Down?

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/toronto-rent-trends-2026/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-21

Toronto rent prices 2026, as of November: what Rentals.ca, liv.rent, TRREB and CMHC show, what a 1-bedroom costs, and the best time of year to sign a lease.

Toronto rent prices in 2026 have stopped falling: as of November 2026, the latest Rentals.ca and Urbanation report shows average asking rents for Toronto apartments and condos up 1.6% in October from a year earlier, the first annual increase in nearly three years. One-bedroom listings, though, are still a little cheaper than in late 2025 in some data. In short, the big discount window of 2024 and 2025 is narrowing, but renters still have more choice than they did a few years ago.

## Key takeaways

- **Toronto's average asking rent rose 1.6% year over year in October 2026** (Rentals.ca and Urbanation, apartments and condos), the first annual increase in nearly three years.
- **The low point came around the turn of the year.** The same report series had Toronto at $2,498 in December 2025, the lowest since early 2022, and $2,482 in February 2026.
- **One-bedrooms are roughly flat.** liv.rent put an unfurnished one-bedroom in the City of Toronto at $1,976 in November 2026, down 1.64% from a year earlier.
- **Vacancy is higher than it was.** CMHC's 2025 survey found Toronto's purpose-built vacancy rate at 3%, the first time at that level since the pandemic.
- **Timing still matters.** Late fall and winter usually bring less competition than the summer and back-to-school rush.

## Toronto rent prices 2026: what the reports say

Different reports measure different things, so it helps to see them side by side. Treat each as one lens, never as "the" Toronto rent.

| Source (period) | What it measures | Latest Toronto figure | Change vs a year earlier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rentals.ca and Urbanation (October 2026) | Average asking rent, apartments and condos, all sizes | — | +1.6% |
| liv.rent (November 2026) | Average asking rent, unfurnished one-bedroom, City of Toronto | $1,976 | -1.64% |
| TRREB (Q2 2026) | Average one-bedroom condo leased through MLS, GTA | $2,273 | -2.3% |
| TRREB (Q2 2026) | Average two-bedroom condo leased through MLS, GTA | $3,013 | -1.7% |
| CMHC (fall 2025 survey) | Purpose-built vacancy rate, Toronto | 3% | Up; first time at 3% since the pandemic |

Why the gap between $1,976 and $2,273 for a one-bedroom? liv.rent tracks listings on its own platform within the City of Toronto, while TRREB tracks condos leased through realtors across the wider GTA, which skews toward newer buildings. Both are useful; just compare like with like.

## Is rent going down in Toronto?

Not much anymore. The steep part of the decline is behind us.

### How we got here

From early 2024 into 2026, Toronto asking rents sat below year-earlier levels month after month. By December 2025, the Rentals.ca and Urbanation average had fallen to $2,498, down 5.1% from a year earlier and almost 12% over two years. In March 2026, Rentals.ca pointed to a surge of new supply, with new condos and purpose-built rental buildings finishing at the same time, as the main driver. Slower population growth, fewer international students and a shaky job market also cut demand.

### What changed this fall

The October 2026 data marked a turn. Toronto's average asking rent rose 1.6% year over year, and three-bedroom units rose faster, up 4.3% to $3,643. Urbanation's president, Shaun Hildebrand, said the window for cheaper rents in Toronto and Vancouver is closing, linking it to fewer new units coming on stream. Nationally, rents were still down 3.2% to $2,036, so Toronto is now moving differently from much of Canada.

### What it means for you

- **Moving soon?** You can still find move-in incentives in some new buildings, but don't assume prices will keep dropping if you wait.
- **Renewing?** Market rents don't change your current lease. For most units first occupied before November 15, 2018, your increase is capped by the [2026 rent increase guideline](/blog/ontario-rent-increase-guideline-2026/) of 2.1%.
- **Bigger units are firming up first.** If you were hoping to share a three-bedroom, start looking early.

## Average rent for a 1-bedroom in Toronto

Depending on the source, a one-bedroom in Toronto typically lists for about $2,000 to $2,300 a month as of late 2026:

- **About $1,976** for an unfurnished one-bedroom in the City of Toronto (liv.rent, November 2026). Furnished one-bedrooms averaged $1,931 in the same report.
- **About $2,273** for a one-bedroom condo leased through MLS across the GTA (TRREB, Q2 2026).

Downtown, newer condos and units with parking or in-suite laundry sit at the top of that range. Older low-rise buildings and units further from the core sit lower. If a solo one-bedroom is a stretch, a room in a shared home is the cheaper route; our guide to the [cost of renting a room in Toronto](/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/) breaks down typical prices and move-in costs.

## Best time of year to rent in Toronto

Toronto's rental market has a clear rhythm, even in a softer year.

### Busy season: May to September

Graduates, students and job movers all hunt at once, so good units go fast. Rentals.ca noted in March 2026 that the summer season usually lifts prices, even if it didn't in 2025. Expect more competition, quicker decisions and fewer concessions.

### Quieter season: November to February

Fewer people move in winter, so landlords with empty units are often more flexible on price, move-in date or extras like parking. The trade-off is fewer listings to choose from, and moving in snow is no fun.

### A simple timing checklist

- Start looking 6 to 8 weeks before your move date.
- Compare the asking rent with at least two reports from the same month.
- Ask whether rent is negotiable, or whether the landlord offers a free month or reduced first month.
- Check whether the unit is covered by rent control before you sign.
- Budget for first month's rent plus a last month's deposit.

## What to watch over the next few months

Rent data moves quickly, so here's when to check back:

- **Early each month:** Rentals.ca and Urbanation publish the National Rent Report, usually in the first week, covering the previous month. This is the quickest read on whether Toronto's October uptick holds.
- **Mid-month:** liv.rent's Ontario report adds a one-bedroom view across about 20 Ontario cities and areas, from Oakville to Oshawa.
- **December:** CMHC usually releases its annual Rental Market Report, with updated vacancy rates for purpose-built rentals.
- **By August 31:** Ontario announces the next year's rent increase guideline, which sets the cap on most renewals for older units.

If several sources point the same way for two or three months in a row, that's a trend. A single month's jump or dip is often just noise.

## How to use these numbers without getting burned

Averages are a starting point, not a price tag. A listing far below the numbers above, especially one where the "landlord" can't show the unit in person, is a classic scam pattern. Neighbourhood also matters more than any citywide figure; see our guide to the [best neighbourhoods to rent in Toronto](/blog/best-toronto-neighbourhoods-for-young-professionals/) for areas that balance price and commute.

## FAQ

**Will Toronto rents go up in 2027?**
Nobody can say for sure. As of the October 2026 data, Urbanation's president said the window for cheaper rents in Toronto is closing as fewer new units arrive, while CMHC expected vacancy to stay near or slightly above 3% through 2026. That points to a flatter market rather than the steady declines of 2024 and 2025.

**Why did Toronto rents fall in 2024 and 2025?**
Analysts point mainly to a wave of new condo and purpose-built rental supply arriving at the same time as slower population growth, fewer international students and a softer job market. More choice gave renters leverage, and asking rents fell for close to three years.

**Does a lower asking rent affect my current lease?**
Not directly. Your rent only changes at renewal, and for most units first occupied before November 15, 2018, increases are capped by Ontario's guideline (2.1% for 2026). Falling market rents mainly help people who are moving or signing a new lease.

**Is it cheaper to rent a room than a 1-bedroom in Toronto?**
Almost always. A one-bedroom typically lists for roughly $2,000 to $2,300 depending on the source, while a room in a shared home usually costs far less. Splitting a two-bedroom with a roommate often lands between the two.

**Where do Toronto rent numbers come from?**
The most quoted are the monthly Rentals.ca and Urbanation National Rent Report, liv.rent's monthly reports, TRREB's quarterly condo rental report and CMHC's annual Rental Market Report. Each measures something different, so always check which source and month a figure comes from.

## Sources

- [CTV News: Average rent in Toronto is at its lowest since early 2022 (Jan 12, 2026)](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/average-rent-in-toronto-is-at-its-lowest-since-early-2022-a-new-report-finds/)
- [CP24: Why are rent prices in Toronto continuing to drop? Experts weigh in (Mar 12, 2026)](https://cp24.com/local/toronto/2026/03/12/why-are-rent-prices-in-toronto-continuing-to-drop-experts-weigh-in)

# 2026多伦多房租走势：房租还在降吗？

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/zh/blog/toronto-rent-trends-2026/
Language: Chinese (Simplified)
Updated: 2026-11-21

2026多伦多房租走势（截至2026年11月）：Rentals.ca、liv.rent、TRREB、CMHC最新数据怎么看，一室一厅多少钱，什么时候租房最便宜，一篇讲清楚。

2026多伦多房租走势一句话概括：跌势基本见底了。截至2026年11月，Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 最新报告显示，10月多伦多公寓（apartment 和 condo）平均挂牌租金比一年前上涨1.6%，是近三年来第一次同比上涨。不过一室一厅的价格在部分数据里仍比2025年底略低，所以现在租房依然比前几年好找，只是"捡便宜"的窗口在慢慢收窄。

## 先看重点

- **10月多伦多平均挂牌租金同比上涨1.6%**（Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation，公寓类，全部房型），是近三年来首次同比上涨。
- **最低点出现在年初前后**：同一系列数据中，2025年12月为2,498加元，是2022年初以来最低；2026年2月为2,482加元。
- **一室一厅基本持平**：liv.rent 数据显示，2026年11月多伦多市不带家具的一室一厅平均1,976加元，同比下降1.64%。
- **空置率比以前高**：CMHC 2025年调查显示，多伦多专门出租楼（purpose-built）空置率为3%，是疫情以来首次达到这个水平。
- **找房时机仍然重要**：秋冬季竞争通常比夏天和开学季小。

## 2026多伦多房租走势：各家报告怎么说？

不同机构统计的东西不一样，放在一起看最清楚。千万别把某一家的平均数当成"多伦多房租"本身。

| 数据来源（时间） | 统计的是什么 | 多伦多最新数字 | 同比变化 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation（2026年10月） | 公寓类平均挂牌租金，全部房型 | — | +1.6% |
| liv.rent（2026年11月） | 多伦多市不带家具一室一厅平均挂牌价 | 1,976加元 | -1.64% |
| TRREB（2026年第二季度） | 大多伦多地区经 MLS 成交的一室公寓平均租金 | 2,273加元 | -2.3% |
| TRREB（2026年第二季度） | 大多伦多地区经 MLS 成交的两室公寓平均租金 | 3,013加元 | -1.7% |
| CMHC（2025年秋季调查） | 多伦多专门出租楼空置率 | 3% | 上升，疫情后首次到3% |

同样是一室一厅，为什么一个1,976、一个2,273？liv.rent 统计的是自己平台上多伦多市范围内的房源；TRREB 统计的是大多伦多地区经地产经纪成交的公寓，新楼比例更高，价格自然偏高。两个数字都有参考价值，关键是同类比较。

## 多伦多房租下降了吗？

简单说：大跌已经过去了，现在是横盘偏稳。

### 这两年房租是怎么跌下来的

从2024年初到2026年，多伦多挂牌租金几乎每个月都低于一年前。到2025年12月，Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 的平均数降到2,498加元，同比下降5.1%，两年累计跌了将近12%。2026年3月，Rentals.ca 方面解释，主要原因是新公寓和专门出租楼集中完工，供应一下子多了；再加上人口增长放缓、国际学生减少、就业市场不稳，需求跟不上。

### 今年秋天出现了什么变化

10月的数据是一个转折：多伦多平均挂牌租金同比上涨1.6%，三室单位涨得更快，上涨4.3%至3,643加元。Urbanation 总裁 Shaun Hildebrand 表示，多伦多和温哥华"房租便宜的窗口正在关闭"，并把原因归于新增供应减少。同期全国平均租金仍同比下降3.2%至2,036加元，可见多伦多已经和加拿大其他很多地方走势不同了。

### 对租客意味着什么

- **近期要搬家**：一些新楼仍有免租期等优惠，但不要指望再等几个月价格会继续大跌。
- **准备续租**：市场价涨跌不影响你现有的租约。2018年11月15日之前首次入住的大多数单位，续租涨幅受 [2026安省涨租上限](/zh/blog/ontario-rent-increase-guideline-2026/) 限制，2026年为2.1%。
- **大户型先回暖**：如果打算几个人合租三室，最好提早开始找。

## 多伦多一室一厅多少钱？

截至2026年11月，按不同来源，多伦多一室一厅挂牌价大约在每月2,000到2,300加元之间：

- **约1,976加元**：多伦多市不带家具一室一厅（liv.rent，2026年11月）；同一报告中带家具的一室一厅平均1,931加元。
- **约2,273加元**：大多伦多地区经 MLS 成交的一室公寓（TRREB，2026年第二季度）。

市中心、新楼、带车位或室内洗衣机的单位通常在区间上端；离市中心远、楼龄较老的低层公寓会便宜一些。如果一个人租一室一厅压力太大，合租单间是最常见的省钱办法，具体价格和入住成本可以看 [多伦多租房多少钱](/zh/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/)。

## 什么时候租房最便宜？

即使在租金偏软的年份，多伦多租房市场也有明显的季节规律。

### 旺季：5月到9月

毕业生、新生、换工作的人都在这段时间找房，好房子很快被抢走。Rentals.ca 在2026年3月提到，夏季租房旺季通常会推高价格（虽然2025年夏天并没有涨）。这时候竞争大、要快速决定，房东也不太愿意让价。

### 淡季：11月到次年2月

冬天搬家的人少，有空房的房东往往更愿意在价格、入住日期或车位等方面让步。缺点是可选房源也少，而且下雪天搬家确实辛苦。对刚落地的新移民和1月入学的留学生来说，这反而是一个机会。

### 找房时间清单

- 提前6到8周开始看房；
- 拿挂牌价和至少两家同月份报告做对比；
- 主动问房东租金能不能谈，有没有免一个月租金或首月优惠；
- 签约前确认这个单位是否受涨租上限保护；
- 预留第一个月房租和最后一个月押金。

## 留学生和新移民现在该怎么做？

房租走稳，不代表找房可以随便。结合现在的市场，给刚来多伦多的朋友几条实用建议：

### 先定预算，再定区域

不要只看全市平均数。先算清楚自己每月能承受的房租（包括水电网、交通和租客保险），再按通勤时间倒推可以住在哪里。沿地铁1号线往北约克方向、2号线往士嘉堡方向多住几站，往往能省下不少钱，通勤时间也还能接受。

### 现在是谈价的好时机

市场还没有完全转热，秋冬淡季房东更愿意谈。可以礼貌地问：租金能不能少一点？能不能包网或送车位？入住日期能不能灵活？很多新楼为了尽快租出去，会给免租期或首月优惠，但一定要把优惠条件写进租约。

### 签约前确认三件事

- **是否受涨租上限保护**：2018年11月15日之后首次入住的单位，续租涨幅一般不受指导线限制，第二年可能涨得比较多。
- **是否使用安省标准租约**：大多数住宅租赁都必须使用政府的标准租约表格。
- **房东是否同住、共用厨卫**：如果和房东本人共用厨房或卫生间，通常不受《住宅租赁法》(RTA) 保护，权益会少很多。

## 接下来要关注哪些数据？

租金数据变化很快，下面这几个时间点值得留意：

- **每月第一周左右**：Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 发布上个月的全国租金报告，这是判断多伦多10月的上涨能不能持续的最快信号。
- **每月中旬**：liv.rent 发布安省报告，覆盖安省约20个城市和地区（从奥克维尔到奥沙瓦），可以看到各地一室一厅的价格。
- **12月**：CMHC 通常会发布年度租赁市场报告，更新专门出租楼的空置率。
- **每年8月31日前**：安省政府公布下一年的涨租指导线，决定大多数老单位续租时最多能涨多少。

如果几家数据连续两三个月指向同一个方向，那才是真正的趋势；某一个月突然涨或跌，往往只是正常波动。

## 怎么用这些数字才不吃亏

平均数只是参考，不是报价。如果一个房源比上面的价格低很多，"房东"又说自己在外地、没法带看，基本可以判断是诈骗套路。微信群、小红书上转来转去的"超低价好房"尤其要小心。另外，具体社区比全市平均数重要得多，同样的预算在北约克、士嘉堡和市中心能租到的房子完全不同。

## 常见问题

**2027年多伦多房租会涨吗？**
没人能打包票。根据2026年10月的数据，Urbanation 总裁认为多伦多"房租便宜的窗口正在关闭"，原因是新完工的房源在减少；CMHC 则预计2026年空置率维持在3%左右或略高。总体看，更可能是横盘或小幅波动，而不是像2024、2025年那样持续下跌。

**为什么2024、2025年多伦多房租一直在跌？**
主要是大量新公寓和专门出租楼在同一时间完工，而人口增长放缓、国际学生减少、就业市场疲软又让需求下降。租客选择多了，议价空间也大了，挂牌租金因此连续下跌了将近三年。

**市场房租降了，我现在的房租会降吗？**
不会自动降。房租只在续租时调整；2018年11月15日之前首次入住的大多数单位，涨幅受安省涨租指导线限制（2026年为2.1%）。市场价下跌主要对正在找房、准备签新约的人有利。

**多伦多合租一个房间比租一室一厅便宜多少？**
通常便宜很多。按不同数据来源，一室一厅挂牌价大约在2,000到2,300加元之间，而合租单间平均远低于这个水平。和一个室友分租两室，人均价格一般介于两者之间。

**网上的多伦多房租数据是哪里来的？**
最常被引用的有：Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation 每月的全国租金报告、liv.rent 每月报告、TRREB（多伦多地区地产局）季度公寓租赁报告，以及 CMHC 每年的租赁市场报告。它们统计口径不同，看数字时一定要注意来源和月份。

## 参考资料

- [Rentals.ca 与 Urbanation：2026年11月全国租金报告（10月数据），Rentals.ca 新闻稿](https://press.rentals.ca/476871-toronto-and-vancouver-rents-post-first-annual-increases-in-more-than-two-and-a-half-years-as-national-decline-narrows)
- [BNN Bloomberg / 加通社：10月全国平均挂牌租金下降3.2%，但多伦多、温哥华上涨（2026年11月5日）](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/real-estate/2026/11/05/average-asking-rents-fall-32-in-october-but-prices-rising-in-toronto-vancouver/)
- [CTV News：多伦多平均租金降至2022年初以来最低（2026年1月12日）](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/average-rent-in-toronto-is-at-its-lowest-since-early-2022-a-new-report-finds/)
- [CP24：多伦多房租为何持续下跌？专家解读（2026年3月12日）](https://cp24.com/local/toronto/2026/03/12/why-are-rent-prices-in-toronto-continuing-to-drop-experts-weigh-in)

# Co-Living vs Renting Alone in Toronto: Which Is Better?

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/co-living-vs-renting-alone-toronto/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

Co-living or a shared rental vs renting alone in Toronto: costs from CMHC data, privacy, flexibility, who is on the lease, who each suits and making it work.

For most people in Toronto, co-living or a shared rental is cheaper than renting alone. CMHC's October 2025 averages put a one-bedroom at $1,761 a month, while half of an average two-bedroom is about $1,023. Renting alone buys privacy, control and simpler legal arrangements. Sharing trades some of that for lower costs and company, and works best when you choose roommates carefully and know who is on the lease.

This guide compares the two on cost, lifestyle, privacy, flexibility and legal protection, and explains who each option suits.

## Key takeaways

- **Sharing usually saves money**, often several hundred dollars a month compared with a one-bedroom.
- **New leases cost more than averages.** CMHC found new tenants pay more than tenants who've stayed put.
- **Privacy and control** are the main reasons to rent alone.
- **Legal protection depends on the setup**, especially whether you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner.
- **Shared living works when expectations match** and are written down.

## What counts as co-living?

People use "co-living" for a few different setups:

- **Co-tenants:** two or more people sign one lease for a whole unit.
- **Renting a room from a tenant:** one person holds the lease and rents rooms to others.
- **Room-by-room rentals:** a landlord or operator rents each bedroom separately, often furnished, with shared common areas. In Toronto, a home where four or more rooms are rented to separate people is a multi-tenant (rooming) house, and the City requires operators to be licensed.
- **Living with the owner:** you rent a room in the owner's home and share their kitchen or bathroom.

Each one comes with different rights, which we cover below.

## Cost: what the data says

### Average rents

U of T Student Life publishes averages from CMHC's October 2025 survey and the City of Toronto's 2026 average market rents:

| Unit type | CMHC average (Oct 2025) | City of Toronto average (2026) |
|---|---|---|
| Room | Not available | $1,146 |
| Bachelor/studio | $1,491 | $1,499 |
| One-bedroom | $1,761 | $1,763 |
| Two-bedroom | $2,045 | $2,055 |

Based on these averages:

- **Renting alone:** about $1,490 for a studio or $1,760 for a one-bedroom.
- **Splitting a two-bedroom:** about $1,020 to $1,030 each.
- **Renting a room:** around $1,150 on the City's figure.

### Why your quote may be higher

These averages include tenants who have lived in their units for years. CMHC's 2025 Rental Market Report found that, on average, new tenants were paying higher rents than sitting tenants. In Toronto, the average rent for a two-bedroom purpose-built unit that changed tenants was **$2,547** in October 2025, down from $2,612 in 2024. Even at that level, two people sharing would pay about $1,274 each, still less than the average one-bedroom.

CMHC also noted more competition from rented condo apartments in Toronto as owners shifted units into the rental market, which gives renters more choice in some areas.

### Other costs to compare

| Cost | Renting alone | Sharing |
|---|---|---|
| Utilities and internet | All yours | Split two or more ways |
| Furniture | Furnish the whole unit | Often only your bedroom; some co-living rooms come furnished |
| Rent deposit | Up to one month of the full rent | Usually your share |
| Household supplies | All yours | Shared |

See our guides to the [cost of renting a room in Toronto](/blog/cost-of-renting-a-room-in-toronto/) and [utilities for Toronto renters](/blog/utilities-for-renters-toronto/) for more detail. CMHC defines housing as affordable when it costs less than 30% of a household's before-tax income, a useful check whichever way you go.

## Lifestyle and privacy

**Renting alone**

- Quiet, your own schedule and your own rules
- Easier for working from home, night shifts, and hosting a partner
- No negotiating over chores, guests or the thermostat
- Can feel isolating, especially for newcomers

**Sharing**

- Built-in company and someone to split chores with
- Bigger or better-located homes become affordable
- Less privacy and more compromise: bathroom schedules, kitchen space, noise
- Your experience depends heavily on who you live with

## Flexibility

- **Renting alone:** you control the lease. To leave, you normally give your landlord 60 days' notice on Form N9, timed to the end of a rental period or the lease term.
- **Co-tenants:** leaving early is harder, because one person's notice can affect everyone on the lease. You'll usually need to agree on a replacement, with the landlord's consent.
- **Renting a room from a tenant, or from the owner:** notice depends on your agreement, which can make moving in and out faster, but also gives you less security.
- **Room-by-room rentals:** each room is often a separate agreement, so a roommate leaving doesn't change your rent.

## Legal differences: who's on the lease

| Setup | Who you deal with | RTA protection | Disputes go to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Renting alone | The landlord | Usually yes | Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) |
| Co-tenants on one lease | The landlord, jointly | Usually yes | LTB for landlord issues; roommate money issues usually go to Small Claims Court |
| Room-by-room lease with a landlord who doesn't live there (including rooming houses) | The landlord | Usually yes | LTB |
| Renting from another tenant | The tenant | Often no | Your agreement; Small Claims Court for money |
| Sharing a kitchen or bathroom with the owner | The owner | Generally no | Your agreement; Small Claims Court for money |

Key points:

- The LTB's guide to the Act says a rental unit can be an apartment, a house, or **a room in a rooming or boarding house**, so renting a single room from a landlord who doesn't live there is usually covered.
- Most Ontario tenancies use the **standard lease**, which says, among other things, that terms banning guests or roommates are void and that assignment or subletting needs the landlord's consent.
- The **Residential Tenancies Act** generally doesn't apply if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or their close family living there. Steps to Justice also notes it might not apply when you share housing with roommates. See [living with your landlord in Ontario](/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/).
- **Co-tenants** are generally each responsible to the landlord for the full rent, so choose people you trust with money.

## Who each option suits

**Renting alone suits you if:**

- You work from home most days or work nights
- You value quiet and routine above savings
- Your income comfortably covers a full unit
- You're in a stable job and plan to stay a while

**Sharing or co-living suits you if:**

- You're a student, newcomer or early in your career
- You want a better location than you could afford alone
- You like company and don't mind compromise
- You want furnished, flexible options while you get settled

## How to make shared living work

1. **Choose roommates on habits, not just availability.** Talk about sleep, cleanliness, guests, money and noise before anyone signs.
2. **Know your setup** before you sign: co-tenant, roommate of a tenant, room-by-room lease, or living with the owner.
3. **Write a [roommate agreement](/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/)** covering rent, bills, chores, guests, quiet hours and moving out.
4. **Split costs fairly.** Bigger rooms or private bathrooms can pay more; see [how to split rent fairly](/blog/split-rent-fairly/).
5. **Keep records** of every payment.
6. **Check in monthly** and fix small issues early.

## Find people before you find a place

## Bottom line

Renting alone costs more but gives you privacy, control and usually full protection under the Residential Tenancies Act. Sharing saves real money, often several hundred dollars a month, and can be a great way to settle into Toronto, as long as you pick compatible people, understand who's on the lease, and put your house rules in writing.

*This article is general information, not legal advice. For your specific situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.*

## FAQ

**Is it cheaper to live with roommates in Toronto?**
Usually, yes. CMHC's October 2025 survey, as summarized by U of T Student Life, put the average Toronto rent at $1,761 for a one-bedroom and $2,045 for a two-bedroom, so splitting a two-bedroom costs about $1,023 each. Rents for new leases are usually higher than these averages, but the gap between sharing and living alone generally remains.

**What is co-living?**
Co-living usually means renting a private bedroom in a shared home, with the kitchen, living room and sometimes bathrooms shared. Some homes are run by an operator who rents each room separately, often furnished; others are simply roommates sharing a regular rental. The legal setup varies, so always check who you're signing with and what you're signing.

**Does the Residential Tenancies Act apply to shared housing?**
Sometimes. It generally doesn't apply if you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's close family who live there. Steps to Justice also notes it might not apply when you share with roommates, for example if you rent from another tenant. If you sign a lease directly with a landlord who doesn't live there, it usually does.

**Who should rent alone in Toronto?**
Renting alone suits people who need quiet and control, such as those working night shifts, working from home most days, or with strong routines, and whose budget can absorb a full unit's rent. CMHC treats housing as affordable when it costs under 30% of before-tax income, a useful check before committing.

**How do I make living with roommates work?**
Choose roommates with similar habits and budgets, agree on house rules before moving in, and write them down in a roommate agreement. Cover rent shares, bills, chores, guests, quiet hours and moving out. Keep payment records, hold a short house meeting each month, and raise small issues early.

## Sources

- [2025 Rental Market Report (CMHC)](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/housing-markets-data-and-research/market-reports/rental-market-reports-major-centres)
- [National Housing Strategy glossary: affordability (CMHC)](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/nhs/guidepage-strategy/glossary)
- [Multi-tenant (rooming) houses (City of Toronto)](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/housing-shelter/rental-housing-rights-information/multi-tenant-rooming-houses/)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies (Steps to Justice)](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)
- [Guide to Ontario's standard lease (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/guide-ontarios-standard-lease)

# Dealing With a Bad Roommate in Toronto: What to Do

URL: https://www.colivease.ca/blog/dealing-with-a-bad-roommate/
Language: English
Updated: 2026-11-03

How to deal with a bad roommate in Toronto: raising noise, mess, unpaid rent and guests, mediation, your legal position by lease type, and when to call police.

Dealing with a bad roommate in Toronto usually comes down to three steps: raise the problem early and specifically, put what you agree in writing, and escalate only if that fails, through mediation, Small Claims Court for money, or the police for safety. Your legal options depend heavily on who is on the lease, so figure that out before you threaten anyone with eviction.

This guide covers the most common roommate problems, how to talk about them, and what the law in Ontario does and doesn't let you do.

## Key takeaways

- **Most problems are fixable with a direct, specific conversation** and a written follow-up.
- **Who is on the lease changes everything.** Co-tenants, roommates who rent from a tenant, and people living with the owner have very different rights.
- **Roommates can't evict co-tenants or change the locks on them.**
- **Money disputes between roommates** usually go to Small Claims Court, not the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB).
- **Safety comes first.** Call 911 if anyone is in danger.

## Common roommate problems and how to raise them

| Problem | What to say or do first | If it keeps happening |
|---|---|---|
| Noise | Agree on quiet hours (for example, 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weeknights) | Write them into your roommate agreement |
| Cleanliness | Propose a rota with named tasks and days | Split the cost of a cleaner, or rebalance chores |
| Unpaid rent or bills | Send the exact amount and a due date in writing | Payment plan, mediation, then Small Claims Court |
| Guests | Agree on notice and overnight limits | Set a rule for when a regular guest pays a share |
| Safety (smoking indoors, unlocked doors, open flames) | Name the risk and the fix | Tell the landlord if it affects the unit; call for help if urgent |

### How to have the conversation

1. **Pick a calm moment.** Not at 1 a.m. in the middle of the noise.
2. **Be specific.** "Dishes have been in the sink since Tuesday" works better than "you're messy."
3. **Say what you need.** "Can we agree the sink is clear before bed?"
4. **Listen.** Your roommate may have a complaint too, or a reason you didn't know about (a new night shift, for example).
5. **Agree on one change and a check-in date.**
6. **Confirm it in writing.** A short message in the group chat creates a record: "As discussed, quiet hours start at 11 p.m. on weeknights."

If you share with several people, a short house meeting once a month can catch small issues before they turn into resentment.

## Put it in writing: the roommate agreement

A written roommate agreement won't bind your landlord, but it gives everyone the same rules and evidence if things go wrong. Cover rent shares, bills, chores, guests, quiet hours and what happens when someone moves out. Our [roommate agreement guide and template](/blog/roommate-agreement-ontario/) walks through each section, and our post on [guest and partner rules](/blog/roommate-guest-rules/) has wording you can copy for the most common flashpoint.

If you didn't write one when you moved in, it's not too late. Suggesting one after a conflict can feel awkward, so frame it as "let's make sure this doesn't happen again" rather than as a punishment.

## Unpaid rent and bills

Money is where roommate problems get serious fastest.

- **Keep records.** E-transfers with notes such as "Nov rent share" and screenshots of bills.
- **Send a clear written request:** what's owed, for what, and by when.
- **Offer a payment plan** if the person is genuinely struggling.
- **Protect the tenancy.** If you're co-tenants, the landlord can generally look to anyone on the lease for the full rent. Paying the shortfall yourself and recovering it from your roommate later may be better than risking arrears.
- **Last resort:** Ontario's Small Claims Court hears claims for money or the return of personal property worth up to $50,000. Your written agreement and payment records will be your main evidence.

## Your legal position depends on who is on the lease

### Co-tenants (you all signed the lease)

You each have a right to live in the unit, and none of you can evict the others. Only the landlord can end a tenancy, and in tenancies covered by the Residential Tenancies Act (RTA), that generally means using an LTB notice and, if the tenant doesn't leave, an LTB hearing. One of the LTB's landlord notices, the N5, covers interfering with others, damage and overcrowding, but an eviction can affect the whole tenancy, so it's rarely a neat way to remove one person.

What this means in practice: with co-tenants, negotiation is usually the only realistic path. Often the best outcome is agreeing that one person leaves and a replacement joins, with the landlord's consent.

### You're the tenant and your roommate rents from you

If you hold the lease and your roommate pays you, they're often treated as an occupant rather than a tenant of the landlord. Steps to Justice notes the RTA might not apply when you share housing with roommates, but the exact answer depends on your facts. That makes your written agreement especially important. If you want them to leave, give clear written notice in line with your agreement (or reasonable notice if it says nothing), and don't change locks or remove their belongings without legal advice. Steps to Justice's free "Do you share rental housing?" tool can help you work out which rules apply.

### You live with the owner

If you share a kitchen or bathroom with the owner, or with the owner's close family who live there, the RTA generally doesn't apply. The LTB can't help either side, and your rights come mainly from your agreement with the owner. See [living with your landlord in Ontario](/blog/living-with-your-landlord-ontario/) for how notice and deposits work in that situation.

## Mediation: a neutral third party

When direct conversations stall, a neutral person can help. Options range from a mutual friend everyone trusts to a community mediation service. Calling 211 connects you with community and social services in Ontario and is a good way to find mediation near you. Mediation works best when both people want to keep living together or want an orderly exit. It's not suitable where there's violence, threats or intimidation.

## When and how to leave

Sometimes the healthiest solution is for someone to move out.

- **Co-tenants:** the N9 is the tenant's notice to end the tenancy. One co-tenant serving an N9 can affect everyone on the lease, so talk to your roommates and the landlord before anyone signs one. A replacement roommate, sublet or assignment needs the landlord's consent. See [ending a tenancy with an N9](/blog/ending-a-tenancy-n9/) for timing.
- **Roommate of a tenant:** follow the notice terms in your roommate agreement and settle your deposit share before you go.
- **Living with the owner:** follow your agreement, or give reasonable notice if it's silent.

Whoever leaves, agree in writing on the move-out date, the final rent and bill shares, and how any deposit contributions are repaid.

## When to call the police or get legal help

**Call 911** if anyone is in immediate danger, there's violence or a threat of violence, someone is breaking in, or there's a fire or medical emergency.

**Call the Toronto Police non-emergency line** for non-urgent crimes, such as a roommate taking your belongings or ongoing harassment.

**Call 211 for a mental health crisis.** The City's Toronto Community Crisis Service sends trained crisis workers, without police, to people 16 and older, 24 hours a day.

**Get legal help** if someone is threatening to lock you out, you're being asked to leave and aren't sure of your rights, or a lot of money is involved. Community legal clinics funded by Legal Aid Ontario give free or low-cost advice; call 1-800-668-8258 or use LAO's online directory. For questions about LTB processes, the LTB's line is 1-888-332-3234.

## Avoid the next bad roommate

## Bottom line

Raise problems early, be specific, and write down what you agree. Know which category you're in, because co-tenants can't evict each other, roommates of a tenant depend on their agreement, and people living with the owner usually fall outside the RTA. Use Small Claims Court for money, the police for safety, and a legal clinic before you take any step you can't undo.

*This article is general information, not legal advice. For your specific situation, contact the Landlord and Tenant Board or a community legal clinic.*

## FAQ

**Can I evict my roommate in Ontario?**
It depends on who is on the lease. If you're co-tenants, you can't evict each other; only the landlord can end a tenancy, normally through the Landlord and Tenant Board. If your roommate pays you and isn't on the lease, the RTA often doesn't apply between you, so your written agreement and reasonable notice matter most. Get legal advice before acting.

**Can I change the locks to keep my roommate out?**
Don't. If your roommate is a co-tenant, they have the same right to live in the unit as you do, and locking them out can create legal trouble for you. Even when the Residential Tenancies Act doesn't apply, removing someone or their belongings without proper notice is risky. Talk to a community legal clinic first.

**What can I do if my roommate won't pay their share of the rent?**
Put the amount owed in writing, keep payment records, and agree on a deadline. If you're co-tenants, the landlord can usually expect the full rent from anyone on the lease, so cover the shortfall if you can to protect the tenancy. You can then try mediation or sue your roommate in Small Claims Court, which hears claims up to $50,000.

**Does the Landlord and Tenant Board handle roommate disputes?**
Generally no. The LTB decides disputes between landlords and tenants under the Residential Tenancies Act. Arguments between roommates about chores, guests or unpaid shares usually aren't LTB matters. Money disputes between roommates normally go to Small Claims Court, and safety issues go to the police.

**When should I call the police about a roommate?**
Call 911 if anyone is in immediate danger, there's violence or a threat of violence, or someone is breaking in. Use the Toronto Police non-emergency line for things like theft of your belongings or ongoing harassment. For a mental health crisis, you can call 211 to reach the Toronto Community Crisis Service.

## Sources

- [Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (Ontario e-Laws)](https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17)
- [Find out if the Residential Tenancies Act applies (Steps to Justice)](https://stepstojustice.ca/steps/housing-law/1-find-out-if-the-residential-tenancies-act-applies/)
- [Do you share rental housing? Interactive tool (Steps to Justice)](https://stepstojustice.ca/resource/do-you-share-rental-housing/)
- [Small Claims Court (Superior Court of Justice)](https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/)
- [Forms: N5 and N9 notices (Landlord and Tenant Board)](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms-filing-and-fees/)
- [Renting in Ontario: Your rights (Government of Ontario)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)
- [Find a legal clinic (Legal Aid Ontario)](https://www.legalaid.on.ca/legal-clinics/)
- [Toronto Community Crisis Service (City of Toronto)](https://www.toronto.ca/community-people/public-safety-alerts/community-safety-wellbeing-programs/toronto-community-crisis-service/)
